title: OMS core & order state machine
body:
## Context
R3 ("Trading on demo", `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7) closes the execution loop, and **E29 is its foundation**: every other trading epic (E30 ticket UI, E31 chart/DOM trading, E32 brackets & native-SL invariant, E33 emulated algos, E34 fan-out, E35 rule engine, E38 paper, E41 journal, E45 resilience) submits orders through the OMS this epic builds. The roadmap starts it on day 1 of S14 and puts it on the critical path `E09 → E27 → E29 → E32 → E34 → E43 → E44` (§11.2).

The design decision is already made and is normative: `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0006-oms-state-machine.md` — an explicit state machine including an `Unknown` state, `orderLinkId` idempotency, and resolution **only** by reconciliation (never blind resubmission). `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §8 is its normative expansion (models, transition rules S1–S9, id scheme, submission pipeline, reconciliation algorithm). `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.5 names the components (`Validator`, `OrderStateMachine`, `Reconciler`, `KillSwitch` hook) inside module **M14**.

The product-visible half of the epic is the **blotters**: SCR-063 (positions · working orders · fills tabs) and SCR-078 (fills/executions detail), plus the reconciliation/desync treatment on SCR-152. These are the screens the owner stares at while money is at risk, so "the app never lies about my book" (US-POS-008) is the epic's real acceptance test.

## Estimate reconciliation (roadmap 42 — engineering 46 — epic 95)
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register (line 129) and §7 R3 scope table (line 377) size E29 at **42 pts**. That roadmap figure prices *engineering* scope only — the OMS build (state machine, submission pipeline, private-stream truth, reconciliation, REST surface) plus the blotter stories — and was never intended to cover the design, QA and security discipline tickets, which the roadmap accounts for separately in the R3 train capacity. The three numbers reconcile exactly, with no scope missing or double-counted:

| Figure | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Roadmap allocation | 42 | Engineering build for M14 + SCR-063/SCR-078, as sized during roadmap planning. |
| Engineering children (`E29-K01`, `E29-T01..T09`, `E29-S01..S08`) | 46 | The same scope, re-estimated at grooming: 46 vs 42 = **+9.5%**, inside the ±15% tolerance of `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §DoR, so the R3 train needs no re-baselining. The delta is the reconciliation UX (`E29-S07`, 5) coming in heavier than the pre-decomposition T-shirt allowed. |
| This epic's `estimate` field | 95 | Per the backlog schema an epic's estimate is the **sum of all children**, which additionally includes the discipline tickets the roadmap line never priced: design `E29-D01..D07` (21), QA `E29-Q01..Q06` (20) and security `E29-X01..X03` (8) = 49. 46 + 49 = 95. |

Roll-up by band (the epic `estimate` field must stay equal to this total — any change requires editing both, and a move of the **engineering** figure outside 36–48 pts requires a roadmap PR, not a silent backlog edit):

| Band | Tickets | Pts |
|---|---|---|
| Spike | K01 | 2 |
| Task (engineering + docs chore) | T01–T09 | 22 |
| Story | S01–S08 | 22 |
| Design | D01–D07 | 21 |
| QA | Q01–Q06 | 20 |
| Security | X01–X03 | 8 |
| **Total (epic estimate)** | **34** | **95** |

Guard: if in-sprint discovery pushes engineering above 48 pts (42 + 15%), the disposition is to descope `E29-S08` (position detail view — US-POS-004 is *Should*) and `E29-S06` (closed positions / daily PnL) into E41 Journal, preserving the Must stories and the critical path `E27 → E29 → E32`.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories — domain POS (all Must/Should) and the OMS-side of domain ORD:**
- US-POS-001 Consolidated positions panel (Must) · US-POS-002 Working orders panel (Must) · US-POS-003 Partial close (Must) · US-POS-004 Position detail view (Should) · US-POS-005 Execution marks on the chart (Must) · US-POS-006 Account and group filtering (Must) · US-POS-007 Position mode and hedge support (Must/Should) · US-POS-008 Reconciliation with the exchange (Must) · US-POS-009 Closed positions and daily PnL (Must)
- Server-side enablement of US-ORD-001 (submit), US-ORD-002 (order types/flags validation) and US-ORD-009/US-ORD-010 (cancel / cancel-all / flatten backends). The **UI** for those lives in E30/E31.

**Screens:** SCR-063 (primary), SCR-078, SCR-152 (reconciling/desync variant), SCR-064 (consumed, owned by E32), SCR-079 (consumed, owned by E27).
**Components:** CMP-114 PositionsGrid, CMP-115 OrderRow, CMP-116 PnLBadge, CMP-123 FlattenAllButton, CMP-129 PositionModeToggle, CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-049/055/056/057 (base table, filter bar, column picker, split button), CMP-076/077/078 (connection, reconnect, stale shade).
**DB tables:** `orders`, `order_events`, `executions`, `positions`, `position_snapshots` (`21-database-schema.md` §3.3.4–3.3.7).
**API:** `GET/POST /orders`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /orders/{orderId}`, `POST /orders/cancel-all`, `GET /orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`, `GET /positions`, `GET /positions/{positionId}`, `POST /positions/{positionId}/close`, `POST /positions/{positionId}/reverse`, `PUT /positions/{positionId}/leverage`, `POST /positions/close-all`, `GET /executions`, `GET /executions/closed-pnl`.
**WS topics:** `orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet` (never throttled, never coalesced — `23-ws-protocol.md` S4/S5).
**Module:** M14 (OMS).

## Out of scope
- Order ticket UI, sizing modes, hotkeys, arm/lock (E30); chart/DOM direct manipulation (E31).
- Bracket objects, scaled ladders and the **enforcement** of the native-SL invariant (E32/M17) — E29 provides the choke point and the `native_stop_required` rejection code but the bracket/partial-fill-aware child sizing is E32's.
- Emulated algos OCO/iceberg/TWAP/chase (E33); trade-group fan-out and the rate-limit governor (E34) — E29 creates the one-leg trade group wrapper only.
- Rule engine (E35–E37), paper matcher (E38), risk caps/kill-switch implementation (E39 — E29 calls its gate), journal (E41), admin screens (E42).
- Live trading. Everything here runs against **Bybit demo (REST-only order entry)**; the live transport path is written behind `ExchangeCapabilities.supports_ws_order_entry` but is gated off until R4/E44.
- Android; separate admin app; non-Bybit venues; non-USDT-linear-perp instruments.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full lifecycle on demo matches the exchange
  Given a demo account with a valid key
  When a limit order is placed, partially filled, amended and finally cancelled
  Then every transition is present in order_events with a monotone seq
  And the local order state equals GET /v5/order/realtime and /v5/order/history for that orderLinkId

Scenario: A lost acknowledgement never duplicates a position
  Given the transport times out after the exchange accepted the order
  When the order enters Unknown and the reconciler runs
  Then the order is resolved to its true exchange state without any resubmission
  And exactly one position exists on the exchange

Scenario: The book is never misreported
  Given local state diverges from the exchange after a 60 s private-WS outage
  When reconciliation completes
  Then exchange truth wins, the correction is audited with both values, and the blotter shows the corrected state within 30 s

Scenario: Order entry is refused when we cannot record it
  Given Postgres is unavailable
  When an order submission is attempted
  Then it is rejected with 503 service_unavailable before any exchange call
```

## Technical notes / design
Pipeline (`24-internal-schemas.md` §8.4): `POST /orders` → RiskGate (E39) → OMS.submit → size/round/validate filters → build `orderLinkId` → INSERT order + `order_events` (write-ahead) → rate budget acquire → adapter send → ack/reject/timeout → private-WS stream applies truth. `orderLinkId = cv{env}-{group22}-{acct4}-{seq2}{purpose2}` ≤36 chars, generated once, reused on every retry.

## Test plan
Unit (state-machine transition matrix incl. every illegal transition), contract (OpenAPI + WS schema), integration against the fixture-replay mock exchange (`packages/fixtures`, `03-testing-strategy.md` §4.1, `rest_*.json` for `/v5/order/realtime`, `/v5/position/list`, `/v5/execution/list`), E2E (Playwright web + Electron over SCR-063), perf (k6 budget #4: submit→ack p95 <300 ms demo, backend-added ≤50 ms), chaos (WS kill mid-order, backend restart, Postgres failover, duplicate acks, out-of-order fills, 10018, 10002).

## Security notes
STRIDE model required before implementation lands (E29-X01). Threats: spoofed order origin, tampered blotter data, repudiation of a placed order, information disclosure of another account's orders (cross-tenant leak), DoS via order flooding, elevation via RBAC scope bypass. Controls: `orders:write`/`positions:write` permissions with `granted_accounts` scope on every route and WS subscription, append-only `order_events`, audit on every mutation, mandatory `Idempotency-Key`, no secret material in diagnostics (redaction). Data classification: **financial / restricted**.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-063 is a real table with `aria-sort`, row-level action menus, totals associated via `scope`; liq-proximity is glyph+text never colour alone; pending/optimistic states are announced in a polite live region; virtualised grid keeps a keyboard-reachable focus model (`05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
Budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2): submit→ack p95 <300 ms on demo, backend-added ≤50 ms p95. Blotter: 500 rows at 60 fps, position updates coalesced at 10 Hz; `orders`/`executions` WS topics never throttled.

## Observability
`order_submit_seconds{transport,env}` (p99 ≤500 ms), `oms_unknown_orders` (gauge, **page if >0 for 60 s**), `oms_reconcile_corrections_total{kind}`, `oms_state_transitions_total{from,to}`, `oms_untracked_orders`, `naked_position_alerts_total`. Audit events: `order.submitted`, `order.amended`, `order.cancelled`, `position.closed`, `oms.reconcile`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Epic-level acceptance verified end-to-end on demo (place → partial fill → amend → cancel → close) with a 48 h continuous run feeding the R3 7-day soak.
- [ ] Coverage ≥90% on M14 packages; zero open P0/P1 against this scope.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green on SCR-063/SCR-078 + one manual screen-reader pass.
- [ ] perf: budget #4 numbers recorded; blotter fps benchmark recorded.
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, all Critical/High closed, Security engineer sign-off (R3 gate, §7.4).
- [ ] QA epic-level regression + exploratory pass recorded.
- [ ] Demoed to Owner and accepted; retro notes filed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E08** (Bybit adapter & ingestion skeleton — the REST/WS client, error taxonomy and fixtures), **E27** (accounts & API-key vault — an OMS with no keys cannot submit), **E09** (auth/RBAC permissions and account scoping), **E17** (WS protocol & framing that the private topics ride on). Consumed by E30, E31, E32, E33, E34, E35, E38, E41, E45.

## Children (mermaid)
```mermaid

  D01[D01 UX research blotters] --> D02[D02 Hi-fi SCR-063]
  D01 --> D03[D03 Hi-fi SCR-078 + desync]

  D03 --> D04
  D04 --> D05[D05 a11y design review]
  D05 --> D06[D06 Handoff]
  T01[T01 Schema & repos] --> T02[T02 orderLinkId]
  T01 --> T03[T03 State machine]
  T02 --> T04[T04 Submission pipeline]
  T03 --> T04
  T03 --> T05[T05 Private WS consumer]
  T04 --> T06[T06 Reconciler]
  T05 --> T06
  T04 --> T07[T07 REST + WS surface]
  T05 --> T07
  T06 --> T08[T08 Unknown/stuck detection & metrics]
  T07 --> S01[S01 Positions tab]
  D06 --> S01
  S01 --> S02[S02 Working orders tab]
  S01 --> S03[S03 Partial close]
  S01 --> S04[S04 Fills tab & SCR-078]
  S04 --> S05[S05 Execution marks]
  S04 --> S06[S06 Closed positions & daily PnL]
  T06 --> S07[S07 Reconciliation UX]
  S01 --> S08[S08 Position detail view]
  S08 --> T09[T09 Docs & ADR reconciliation]
  X01[X01 STRIDE] --> T04
  X01 --> X02[X02 Abuse cases & SAST]
  X02 --> X03[X03 Security sign-off]
  Q01[Q01 Test plan] --> Q02[Q02 E2E]

  Q01 --> Q04[Q04 Chaos]
  Q01 --> Q05[Q05 a11y audit]

  S07 --> D07[D07 Design QA]
```

## Risks
R7 Data accuracy (a wrong blotter is worse than no blotter), R3 Real-time cost, R11 Alert reliability (Unknown-order paging), R6 Feed rot (Bybit schema drift), R5 Scope (fan-out/algos pressure to creep in from E33/E34).

## Branch

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: UX research: what traders need from a positions and orders blotter
body:
## Context
SCR-063 is the screen the owner watches while money is at risk, and E29 is the first epic to build it. Before wireframes we must know what a blotter has to answer at a glance, what "pending" must look like when an amend is in flight, and how a reconciliation correction should be told to a user who may have acted on the wrong number a second earlier. Net-new interaction ⇒ research first per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 and the design-ahead rule (≥2 sprints before the S15/S16 build).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Research plan + 3–5 moderated sessions with the Owner and account-manager personas (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`) using competitor blotters (TradingView, Bybit web, DeepCharts) as think-aloud props.
- Answer with evidence, for SCR-063 / SCR-078:
  - Default column set and order for the **Positions**, **Working orders**, **Fills** tabs (candidate columns are enumerated in `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-063); what may be hidden behind CMP-056 ColumnPicker.
  - Default grouping (account vs symbol vs trade group) and whether the totals row is expected to aggregate across environments (it must not — demo and live are never summed).
  - How an **optimistic/pending** amend must read so nobody believes a stop moved when it did not (ADR-0006 rule S2 / `24-internal-schemas.md` S2).
  - How a **reconciliation correction** should be surfaced (inline row flash vs banner vs both) and what text makes "the exchange disagreed with us and won" understandable.
  - Liquidation-proximity escalation thresholds and wording (must be text+glyph, never colour alone).
  - What US-POS-004 position detail must contain to be worth opening.
- Written findings note + a decision table appended to the SCR-063 catalogue entry, signed by the Owner.

## Out of scope
Visual design (D02/D03), any implementation, the order ticket (E30).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Column set decided
  Given competing column sets from three reference tools
  When research completes
  Then one default column set per tab is chosen, recorded in a decision table, and written into 14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-063

Scenario: Pending semantics agreed
  When participants are shown three candidate treatments for an in-flight amend
  Then the chosen treatment is one that no participant misread as "already applied"

Scenario: Correction wording tested
  Given a simulated reconciliation correction
  When shown to participants
  Then at least 4 of 5 correctly state what changed, which value is now true, and that the exchange is authoritative
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the R2 builds as props where possible; no new prototype code. Record sessions per `ADR-0015-recording-policy.md` (consent, retention).

## Test plan
N/A — research. Findings are validated later by D07 design QA and Q05 a11y audit.

## Security notes
No production keys or real balances in props; use demo/fixture data only. Session recordings stored per the recording policy, deleted after synthesis.

## Accessibility notes
Include at least one session covering keyboard-only and screen-reader expectations for a dense grid; feed results into D05.

## Performance notes
Capture the density expectation (how many rows must be readable at once) so the virtualisation budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` is driven by a real number.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings note merged under `docs/plan/` and linked from SCR-063.
- [ ] Decision table signed by the Owner and the CDO.
- [ ] D02/D03 tickets updated with the decisions as constraints.
- [ ] Presented at Design Review.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E27 — account/environment vocabulary (which accounts, demo vs live badging) must exist before blotter grouping can be researched.

## Branch
`design/oms-core-blotter-research`

## Context
SCR-063 (`14-screens-catalogue.md` §5, wireframe ref R-130) is the primary surface of E29 and is consumed by E30/E31/E32/E34 for flatten, reverse and group views. It must be designed once, completely, including the unhappy states, because every trading epic inherits it.

- Figma frames, light and dark, comfortable and compact density, for SCR-063:

  - Working-orders tab: account, symbol, side, type, qty, filled qty, price, trigger, TIF, flags, age, parent algo/bracket; untriggered conditionals in a distinct section.
  - Inline amend affordance with an explicit **pending** treatment (US-POS-002) and the "amend rejected — your order is unchanged" resolution.
  - Row actions: Close 25 % / 50 % / Close / Reverse / SL/TP / Chart (CMP-057 SplitButton).
  - Totals row, group-by control, CMP-055 FilterBar with removable chips (US-POS-006), CMP-056 ColumnPicker, CSV export.
  - States: loading · empty ("No open positions") · reconciling · desync warning banner · liq-proximity warning rows · frozen/lockout (actions disabled **with reasons**) · viewer read-only · mixed-environment rows with per-row DEMO/LIVE badge.

title: Hi-fi: SCR-078 fills detail and the reconciling/desync states on SCR-152
body:
## Context
US-POS-005 and US-POS-009 need a fills surface (SCR-078), and US-POS-008 needs the app to tell the truth when it has just been corrected by the exchange — which is the reconciling/desync variant of SCR-152 plus the per-panel stale treatment (CMP-078 StaleDataShade).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Figma frames for **SCR-078 Fills / executions detail** (drawer): per-fill rows (time, price, qty, fee, fee currency, maker/taker, order id, exec id, trade group, causing rule, journal link), aggregation to an average price with maker/taker split, slippage vs intended price where an intent exists, fan-out grouping by account, CSV export, empty state — satisfying the SCR-078 sign-off checklist.
- Figma frames for the **reconciling** and **desync** states used by E29: the SCR-152 banner variant ("Reconciling with the exchange…"), the SCR-063 amber desync banner ("Position data is being verified — actions temporarily limited"), the per-account **stale** treatment that disables order entry for that account after repeated reconciliation failure (US-POS-008 scenario 3), and the post-reconnect summary ("While you were offline: 1 order filled, 1 stop moved by a rule").
- Copy deck for every message above, reviewed with the Owner; wording must name which value is now authoritative.

## Out of scope
SCR-063 itself (D02); the connection/reconnect machinery visuals owned by the platform epics — this ticket only adds the OMS-specific variants.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Correction is explained, not hidden
  Given local state was corrected by reconciliation
  Then the design shows both the previous and the corrected value and states that the exchange is authoritative

Scenario: Stale account blocks entry visibly
  Given reconciliation has failed for 2 minutes on account B
  Then account B's rows are marked stale and every order-entry control for it is drawn disabled with the reason in text

Scenario: Fills drawer sign-off checklist satisfied
  When the CDO reviews SCR-078 against its catalogue checklist
  Then all six items pass
```

## Technical notes / design
Reuse CMP-028 Callout, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-049 Table, CMP-076/077/078, CMP-099 PrintExportBar, CMP-116 PnLBadge. No new components unless raised into D04.

## Test plan
Design review + copy review with the Owner; verified by D07 and by Q02 E2E assertions on the exact strings.

## Security notes
Fills expose financial data only; no key material, no exchange signature, and order diagnostics deep-links must be marked as audited-on-read.

## Accessibility notes
Banner is `role="alert"` once then persistent; countdowns are not announced per tick; fee/funding values carry sign and currency in the accessible name.

## Performance notes
Fills list is virtualised and coalesced to 5 Hz; 1 000-fill session must render without exceeding 4 ms scripting per frame — the design must not require per-row measurement.

## Observability
Spec marks `execution.detail_viewed`, `execution.exported` analytics events.

title: Design-system contributions and motion spec for blotter components
body:
## Context
SCR-063/SCR-078 introduce or materially extend five catalogued components. They must land in the design system (and Storybook) rather than as one-off screen code, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Design-system entries, props and states for: **CMP-114 PositionsGrid** (extends CMP-049 with liq-proximity warning rows), **CMP-115 OrderRow** (incl. pending/optimistic and rejected variants), **CMP-116 PnLBadge** (sign, currency, R-multiple), **CMP-123 FlattenAllButton** (destructive, hold-to-confirm variant), **CMP-129 PositionModeToggle** (one-way/hedge, disabled-with-reason variant), plus the reuse contract for **CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect**.
- Motion spec: row insert/remove, value-change flash (must be perceivable without colour, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`), pending shimmer, correction flash on a reconciled row. Durations and easing from `16-design-system-brief.md`; nothing longer than 200 ms on a data row.
- Update `15-component-catalogue.md` entries with the final props/a11y/token lines.

## Out of scope
Implementation of the components (done inside E29-S01/S02) and Storybook code (belongs to the implementing story).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No orphan component
  When the SCR-063 and SCR-078 specs are cross-checked against 15-component-catalogue.md
  Then every element maps to a catalogued component with defined props and states

Scenario: Motion is reduced-motion safe
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then every specified animation has a defined non-animated equivalent that still conveys the change

Scenario: Destructive control is specified once
  Then FlattenAllButton's confirm behaviour is specified in the design system and referenced, not redefined, by E30/E31/E39
```

## Technical notes / design
Value-change flash must be paired with a text/glyph delta so it survives colour-blindness and reduced motion.

## Test plan
Design-system review; later verified by axe-core in CI and by D07.

## Security notes
N/A.

## Accessibility notes
Every component entry states keyboard model, accessible name composition, and live-region policy (row updates are **not** announced individually; only state changes the user requested are).

## Performance notes
Motion must be compositor-only (transform/opacity); no layout-thrashing animation on a virtualised list.

## Observability
N/A.

title: Accessibility design review of the blotters and correction messaging

## Context
A dense, high-frequency financial grid is one of the hardest a11y surfaces in the product, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 explicitly removes any "internal tool" exemption. Reviewing at design time is far cheaper than retrofitting after S16.

## Scope / Deliverables
- WCAG 2.2 AA design review of SCR-063, SCR-078 and the reconciling/desync/stale states, producing a written findings list with severity and an owner per finding.
- Verify and record: keyboard model for a virtualised grid (roving tabindex, page/home/end, column-header sort activation), focus preservation across data updates (focus must never be stolen or lost when a row re-sorts), accessible names for every action in a row menu, live-region policy (what is announced, what is not), contrast for all states incl. disabled-with-reason, target size ≥24×24 px for row actions (WCAG 2.2 2.5.8), and text alternatives for liq-proximity and pending signals.
- Define the screen-reader script that Q05 will execute.

## Out of scope
The implementation audit (E29-Q05) and axe-core wiring (CI, E03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Focus survives an update
  Given focus is on a row action while a position update re-sorts the grid
  Then the specified behaviour keeps focus on the same logical row and this is written into the spec

Scenario: Nothing depends on colour alone
  When every state in the specs is audited

Scenario: Findings closed

```

Follow the "data grid" pattern of `05-accessibility-standard.md`; the canvas-surrogate pattern (§6.1) does **not** apply here — SCR-063 is real DOM.

Manual design audit + the contrast checker; output becomes the Q05 script.

N/A.

The chosen keyboard model must not force rendering of off-screen rows; specify how virtualisation and roving focus coexist.

N/A.

## Scope / Deliverables

- Verify destructive/confirm affordances (close, close-all, reverse entry points hosted here) match the design-system contract from D04.
- File discrepancies as Bugs with `priority/*` set; re-verify fixes.

## Out of scope
Functional testing (Q-series) and a11y auditing (Q05) — though findings are cross-linked.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Token fidelity
  When the built screens are inspected
  Then no hard-coded colour, spacing or type value is present where a token exists

Scenario: States match
  Given each state in the state matrix is forced in the test environment

Scenario: Sign-off
```

## Performance notes

title: Spike: measure the Bybit demo order path and private-WS parity before the OMS is built
body:
## Context
ADR-0006 §Validation calls for a private-WS soak ("Spike S3: 24 h soak of the private WS client on demo with zero missed executions") before the OMS commits to "the WS stream, never the REST ack, is the source of truth". Two numbers decide the shape of the implementation and must be measured, not assumed:
1. The Bybit **demo** REST round-trip for `/v5/order/create`, because budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2) allocates ≤250 ms of the 300 ms p95 to it and only ≤50 ms to us.
2. Whether the demo private stream (`stream-demo`) delivers `order`, `execution.fast`, `position` and `wallet` with the ordering and completeness ADR-0006 assumes. Demo has **no WS order entry** (locked decision) but does have private streams.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Throwaway harness on branch `spike/oms-demo-path` (not merged) using the E08 adapter to place → partially fill → amend → cancel ≥200 small orders on a demo account across ≥4 h, plus a 24 h idle private-WS soak.
- Measure and record:
  - REST `/v5/order/create` RTT distribution (p50/p95/p99) from the backend host to `api-demo.bybit.com`.
  - Private-WS event latency from exchange `execTime`/`updatedTime` to local receipt; count of executions seen **only** via `GET /v5/execution/list` backfill (target zero).
  - Observed ordering — does an `execution` ever arrive after the `order` transition it caused? `23-ws-protocol.md` S5 requires we emit execution→order→position, so a violation means T05 needs a causal reorder buffer.
  - Exact shapes of `retCode` 10018 (rate limit), 10002 (clock drift) and duplicate-`orderLinkId` (10001/110072) responses.
  - Demo 7-day order-retention behaviour (`24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3 rule 6).
- Contribute the captured sequences to `packages/fixtures` (`rest_*.json` + private `*.jsonl.gz`) for the integration suite.

## Out of scope
Any production code. Live-environment measurement (R4/E44). WS order entry (unavailable on demo).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Budget feasibility answered
  When the REST RTT distribution is measured
  Then the spike states, with numbers, whether budget #4 (p95 <300 ms end-to-end on demo) is achievable with ≤50 ms backend overhead

Scenario: Source-of-truth assumption validated
  Given a 24 h private-WS soak
  Then the count of executions seen only via REST backfill is reported
  And if it is non-zero the reconciliation cadence is revised in ADR-0006 before T06 starts

Scenario: Error shapes captured
  Then fixtures exist for 10018, 10002 and duplicate-orderLinkId responses
  And the E08 adapter error taxonomy is confirmed or an amendment ticket is filed
```

## Technical notes / design
Timebox **4 working days** plus the unattended 24 h soak. Decision rule agreed up front: if demo REST p95 exceeds 250 ms, budget #4 is renegotiated in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` rather than silently absorbed by shrinking our 50 ms. If ordering violations are observed, E29-T05 gains a reorder buffer keyed on `(ts_exec, seq)`.

## Test plan
The spike is itself measurement. Outputs feed E29-Q03 (perf scripts) and the fixtures used by T04/T05/T06.

## Security notes
Demo keys only, withdrawal permission OFF, IP-whitelisted, obtained from the E27 vault — never a live key and never a key committed to the branch. Captured fixtures are scrubbed of keys, signatures and account identifiers before commit (`03-testing-strategy.md` §4.1). CI must not be able to reach `api-demo.bybit.com`; this harness runs manually on the dev host only.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
Produces the baseline numbers against which budget #4 is gated in E29-Q03.

## Observability
The harness exports the production metric names (`order_submit_seconds`) so Grafana panels can be built against real data before the OMS exists.

title: Create the OMS schema migration and repositories for orders, events, executions, positions
body:
## Context
`24-internal-schemas.md` rule S7 makes Postgres authoritative: "If Postgres is unavailable, order entry is blocked — we never accept an order we cannot durably record." Nothing else in E29 can start until the tables and repositories exist exactly as specified in `21-database-schema.md` §3.3.4–3.3.7.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration creating (or extending where E27/E28 already created `exchange_accounts` / `trade_group_legs` and shared enums): `orders`, `order_events`, `executions`, `positions`, `position_snapshots`, plus enums `order_state`, `order_intent`, `order_event_kind`.
- Every constraint and index from the DDL verbatim — notably `ux_orders_link` (unique `order_link_id`), `ux_orders_exch_id`, `ix_orders_open`, `ix_orders_inflight`, `ix_orders_untracked`, `ord_link_fmt` CHECK (both arms exactly as in `21-database-schema.md` §3.3.4; the format is owned by `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3), the `leaves_qty` STORED generated column, `ux_exec_id` unique `(exchange_account_id, exec_id)`, and `ix_pos_no_sl`.
- Append-only enforcement: `forbid_mutation()` triggers `trg_oe_append` on `order_events` and `trg_exec_append` on `executions`.
- Repository layer in module **M14**: `OrderRepository`, `OrderEventRepository`, `ExecutionRepository`, `PositionRepository`, `PositionSnapshotRepository` — async SQLAlchemy Core, `Decimal` end to end (never `float`), all writes in an explicit transaction, executions inserted with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
- `PositionRepository.list_unprotected()` backed by `ix_pos_no_sl` (open position with no exchange-side stop) — the query behind the naked-position alert.
- Down-migration plus a migration test that applies and reverts against empty and populated databases.

## Out of scope
Business logic (T03/T04). Monthly partitioning of `order_events` (deferred until >20 M rows; filed as a later chore). Parquet export of detached partitions (E41). Trade-group tables (E28/E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Idempotency is enforced by the database
  Given an order with order_link_id "cvl-0TLr6mSAQFGvyfsJ0nLDCh-d0hb-00en" exists
  When a second insert with the same order_link_id is attempted
  Then the unique index rejects it and the repository raises DuplicateOrderLinkId

Scenario: History cannot be rewritten
  When an UPDATE or DELETE is attempted on order_events or executions
  Then the forbid_mutation trigger raises and the transaction aborts

Scenario: Fills deduplicate across sources
  Given execution exec_id "E1" for account A is already stored
  When the same exec_id arrives again from the WS stream and again from REST backfill
  Then exactly one row exists

Scenario: Monetary precision is preserved
  When qty 0.000000000000000001 and price 63099.80 are round-tripped
  Then the values return byte-identical as Decimal with no float in the path
```

## Technical notes / design
Numeric columns are `numeric(38,18)`; a `Decimal` type decorator maps them, and a Semgrep rule forbids `float(` on any OMS monetary value. `leaves_qty` is read-only in the mapper (generated column). Config keys: `CV_DB_DSN`, `CV_DB_POOL_MIN/MAX`, `CV_OMS_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 2000).

## Test plan
Unit: CRUD per repository; constraint-violation cases (negative qty, `cum_exec_qty > qty`, malformed `order_link_id`, illegal `position_idx`, bad TIF); dedupe path; append-only triggers. Integration: `testcontainers-python` Postgres 16, migration up/down, index-presence assertions, `EXPLAIN` assertion that `list_open_orders` uses `ix_orders_open` and `list_unprotected` uses `ix_pos_no_sl`. Coverage ≥90%.

## Security notes
`order_events.payload` stores raw exchange messages and **must be redacted of credentials and signatures before insert** (`21-database-schema.md` §3.3.5): implement `redact_exchange_payload()` and unit-test it against a fixture containing `X-BAPI-SIGN`, `X-BAPI-API-KEY` and a recv-window header. Data classification financial/restricted. Every read helper takes an account-scope argument; no unscoped `select(orders)` helper is exported (defence in depth behind the RBAC layer). Label `security`: migration touches financial records.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
Open-order and open-position lookups must be index-only over the partial indexes (asserted in an integration test). The hot submit path writes the order row and its first `order_events` row in a single transaction/round trip.

## Observability
`oms_db_write_seconds{table}` histogram; `order_link_id` logged on every write for correlation.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified by an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§4.2).
- [ ] Coverage: touched backend/OMS packages ≥90% line (local R3 policy for OMS/risk modules, `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4), frontend ≥80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated: `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md` / `21-database-schema.md` reflect shipped behaviour; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] Security: SAST (Bandit/Semgrep/CodeQL) + SCA clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present (mandatory — `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8, order-placement path).
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario.

- [ ] PR(s) merged through the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner; PR ≤400 LOC diff preferred.

title: Implement the orderLinkId generator, collision check and adoption rules
body:
## Context
`orderLinkId` is the single mechanism that structurally prevents duplicate positions (ADR-0006 decision rule 1; `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3). It is also the correlation key for logs, metrics exemplars, audit, journal, reconciliation and UI deep links, so it must be generated exactly once and never mutated.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `OrderLinkId` value object and generator in M14 implementing the scheme from `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3:
  `{prefix:2}{env:1}-{group22}-{acct4}-{seq2}{suffix:2}` = 36 chars total, e.g. `cvl-0TLr6mSAQFGvyfsJ0nLDCh-d0hb-00en`.
  - `prefix` = `cv`; `env` ∈ `l` live / `d` demo / `t` testnet / `p` paper; `group22` = base62 of the trade-group UUID padded to 22; `acct4` = `base62(crc32(str(account_id).lower()) mod 62^4)`, zero-padded to 4 (a diagnostic tag only); `seq2` = base62 leg/child sequence 0–3843; `suffix` = purpose tag `en|sl|tp|sc|fl|ac`.
- Generation rules: generated **once before the first send**, persisted immediately, reused unchanged on every retry; amends never change it; cancel-and-replace algos allocate a new id with incremented `seq2` and record `replaces_order_id`.
- Collision check at generation: if any local row, in any state, already has the id, increment `seq2` and retry (16 increments, never past `seq2` = 3843, then raise a typed `OrderLinkIdExhausted`).
- **Success-after-lookup** rule: a duplicate-id rejection from the exchange (retCode 10001 duplicate message, or 110072) is *not* an error — query `GET /v5/order/realtime` then `/v5/order/history` for that id and adopt the true state (`20-architecture.md` §9, `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3 rule 3).
- Demo-retention rule: on demo, an id older than 6 days is unresolvable-by-history; the reconciler closes it as `Rejected` with `reject_code=DEMO_RETENTION_EXPIRED` (implemented here as a policy object consumed by T06).
- Parser/validator so any stored id can be decomposed back into `(env, group, account, seq, purpose)` for diagnostics.
- `OUR_ID` and `EXT_ID` (the two `ord_link_fmt` arms, applied with `re.fullmatch`) and `ext_key(orderId)` for adopted rows, in `candleviewer.domain` beside the `OrderLinkId` primitive, so the Bybit adapter can normalise ids without importing M14 (`24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3, §14.2 rule 11).

## Out of scope
The reconciliation loop itself (T06); trade-group creation (E28/E34 — this task consumes a group UUID, creating a one-leg group is T04's job).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Deterministic and bounded
  Given a trade group, an account and a purpose
  When the id is generated twice for the same leg and sequence
  Then both results are identical, 36 characters, and match ^cv-?[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ within Bybit's charset

Scenario: Retry reuses the id
  Given a submission timed out after send
  When the submission is retried
  Then the same order_link_id is sent, so the exchange deduplicates instead of creating a second order

Scenario: Duplicate rejection is adopted, not failed
  Given Bybit rejects a create with a duplicate-orderLinkId code
  When the OMS handles it
  Then it queries realtime then history for that id and adopts the returned state rather than reporting an error to the user

Scenario: Local collision is caught
  Given an id already exists locally, in any state
  When generation is attempted for the same tuple
  Then seq2 is incremented and the collision is logged at warning with both ids
```

## Technical notes / design
Base62 alphabet `0-9A-Za-z`; UUID→base62 via big-integer conversion, zero-padded left to 22. `crc32` over the canonical lowercase UUID string. The generator is pure and total — no I/O except the collision check, which is a single indexed lookup on `ux_orders_link`. Environment character is taken from the account's environment, never from a global — a paper order and a demo order for the same group must differ.

## Test plan
Unit: length invariant across 10 000 random UUIDs/accounts (property test); charset invariant; determinism; collision-increment path; parser round-trip; env character mapping for all four environments; purpose-suffix mapping for all six purposes. Contract: the id satisfies the `ord_link_fmt` CHECK from T01. Integration: duplicate-rejection adoption against the K01 fixture. Coverage ≥95% on this module (it is small and critical).

## Security notes
The id embeds no secret and no user identifier — only opaque base62 of internal UUIDs and a CRC. Confirm in review that account *names* never leak into it (an id is visible to the exchange). Threat: an attacker able to *predict* another user's id could, with `orders:write` on that account, attempt a colliding submit — this is defended by RBAC scope, not by unpredictability, and is recorded as an accepted design note in E29-X01.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI. (The id is surfaced in diagnostics; its presentation is E30/E31's concern.)

## Performance notes
Generation must be <50 µs excluding the collision lookup; it sits on the hot submit path inside the ≤50 ms backend budget.

## Observability
Every log line, span and audit record on the order path carries `order_link_id` as a structured field; it is used as the Prometheus exemplar label on `order_submit_seconds`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified by an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§4.2).

title: Implement the canonical order state machine with write-ahead events
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B1). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. The `frozenset` transition table, `IllegalTransition` and S6 terminal immutability become the chart plus `strict`. S1-S9 bindings, `apply_execution` and the write-ahead `CvAuditPlugin` wiring stay.

## Context
This is the heart of ADR-0006 and `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.2. Every order-affecting path in the product — ticket, chart, DOM, hotkey, rule, algo child, fan-out leg, paper matcher — converges here, so the transition table must be exhaustive and the illegal transitions must be impossible rather than merely unused.

## Scope / Deliverables
- State set and transition graph are defined by `statechart/machines/B01.order.machine.json` (catalogue §B1), matching `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.2 exactly: `draft, validated, submitting, submitted, partially_filled, filled, cancel_pending, cancelled, amend_pending, rejected, expired, triggered, unknown, untracked`.
- Illegal transitions are impossible by chart construction (`strictTargets`, `strict_config`); the chart's guarded-fallthrough arms audit every denied attempt, never silently ignoring it.
- Binding rules S1–S9 implemented and individually unit-tested:
  - **S1** `unknown` on any post-send transport failure; **no** resubmission from `unknown`.
  - **S2** amend rejection leaves the prior order live and unchanged, and emits an explicit `amend_rejected` event for the UI.
  - **S3** a fill arriving in `cancel_pending` wins the race → `partially_filled`/`filled`.
  - **S4** executions deduped by `exec_id`; a repeat never double-counts `filled_qty`.
  - **S5** out-of-order private pushes ordered by `(ts_exec, seq)`; a push older than `last_exchange_update` is ignored **except** fills, which are always applied.
  - **S6** terminal states are immutable; a post-terminal push raises `ReconcileAnomaly`, is audited and alerted, and does not mutate the order.
  - **S7** Postgres authoritative — if the event write fails, the in-memory state is not changed.
  - **S8** write-ahead: the append-only `order_events` row is written **before** the in-memory transition.
  - **S9** `untracked` for orders discovered on the exchange that we never created — displayed, adoptable, never auto-managed by rules.
- `apply_execution(execution)` computing `cum_exec_qty`, `cum_exec_value`, `avg_price`, `fee_paid` and deriving the resulting state.
- Deterministic replay: given an `order_events` stream, rebuilding the order yields byte-identical state (used for crash recovery and diagnostics).
- Implement the `B1` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B01.order.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('order', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/01_order.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_01_order.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
Transport/submission (T04), private-stream consumption (T05), reconciliation (T06), rate budgeting (E34), risk gate (E39), the native-SL guard's bracket-aware logic (E32 — T03 only exposes the `native_stop_required` rejection path).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The whole transition matrix is covered
  Given every ordered pair of states
  When a transition is attempted
  Then exactly the pairs listed in 24-internal-schemas.md §8.2 succeed and every other pair raises IllegalTransition

Scenario: Cancel loses the race to a fill
  Given an order in cancel_pending
  When a full execution arrives
  Then the order becomes filled, the cancel result is recorded as lost-race, and no error is surfaced to the user

Scenario: Amend rejection does not move the stop
  Given an order in amend_pending with price 63000
  When the exchange rejects the amend
  Then the order returns to its prior live state with price 63000 and an amend_rejected event is emitted

Scenario: Duplicate fill never double-counts
  Given execution E1 for 0.1 has been applied
  When E1 is delivered a second time
  Then filled_qty is unchanged

Scenario: Terminal state is immutable
  Given a filled order
  When a further exchange push arrives for it
  Then a ReconcileAnomaly is raised, audited and alerted, and the order is unchanged

Scenario: Crash recovery is deterministic
  Given an order_events stream for an order
  When the order is rebuilt from events alone
  Then the resulting state equals the state before the simulated crash
```

## Technical notes / design
Pure-ish core: `apply(event) -> (new_state, list[SideEffect])`; persistence is injected, so the machine is unit-testable without a database. Write-ahead ordering is enforced by construction — the persistence adapter returns only after the event row is committed. `ReconcileAnomaly` raises the `oms.reconcile_anomaly` audit event and increments a counter that alerts. Error codes exposed: `ILLEGAL_TRANSITION`, `UNRESOLVED_AFTER_RECONCILE`, `DEMO_RETENTION_EXPIRED`, `NATIVE_STOP_REQUIRED`, `POST_TERMINAL_PUSH`.
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B1.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
Unit: full N×N transition matrix (table-driven); S1–S9 each with a dedicated test; execution accumulation arithmetic with `Decimal` including partial→partial→full; out-of-order and duplicate pushes; property test that no event sequence can produce `filled_qty > qty`. Integration: rebuild-from-events against a populated Postgres. Model-based test (hypothesis stateful) driving random legal event sequences and asserting the invariants `0 ≤ filled_qty ≤ qty`, `terminal ⇒ immutable`, `event.seq` monotone. Coverage ≥95%.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B1.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
Repudiation is the primary threat: `order_events` is the non-repudiation record, so the write-ahead rule and the append-only trigger are security controls, not just correctness ones. Every transition records `source` ∈ `local|rest|ws_private|reconcile|paper` — a transition claiming an exchange source must carry the raw payload (redacted) that justifies it. Review for injection via exchange-supplied `retMsg` stored in `reject_message` (stored as text, never interpolated into SQL or rendered as HTML).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI. State names surfaced to the UI must have human-readable labels defined in the copy deck (E29-D06).

## Performance notes
A transition (including the event write) must complete in ≤5 ms p95 so it fits inside the ≤50 ms backend portion of budget #4. The machine holds no global lock — concurrency is per-order via a keyed lock on `order_id`.

## Observability
`oms_state_transitions_total{from,to,source}`, `oms_illegal_transitions_total` (alert >0), `oms_reconcile_anomaly_total` (alert >0), span per transition with `order_link_id` exemplar.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified by an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§4.2).

- [ ] Security: SAST (Bandit/Semgrep/CodeQL) + SCA clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present (mandatory — `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8, order-placement path).

> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B1). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. Transport and rounding. It sends via the gateway only.

## Context
`24-internal-schemas.md` §8.4 specifies the submit path end to end. It is the single choke point through which *every* order in the product passes, which is precisely why the safety invariants are enforced here and not at call sites (`32-risk-register.md` mitigation for the native-SL risk).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `OMS.submit(intent, ctx)` implementing the §8.4 sequence: RiskGate check → size & round → validate instrument filters → build `orderLinkId` → INSERT order (`state=validated`) + event → rate-budget acquire → `state=submitting` + event → adapter `place_order` → branch on ack / business reject / transport error → persist outcome.
- `Validator` (`20-architecture.md` §3.5): instrument filters from `GET /instruments` (tick size, `qty_step`, min/max qty, min notional, max leverage), RBAC account scope, **environment match** (an order for a demo account can never be routed to live), kill-switch state (E39 gate — called, not implemented here), per-account profile symbol allow-list (E28), Postgres availability (S7).
- Error taxonomy surfaced as API error codes exactly as in `22-api-openapi.yaml`: `tick_size_violation`, `lot_size_violation`, `risk_limit_breached`, `native_stop_required`, `trading_disabled`, `RATE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` → 429, `exchange_error` → 502, `service_unavailable` → 503.
- Single-account convenience wrapper: `POST /orders` creates a **one-leg trade group** internally so single and fanned-out orders share one state machine, audit trail and journal linkage (`22-api-openapi.yaml` `/orders` description).
- `Idempotency-Key` handling: required on every mutating trading route; for `POST /orders` the server stores it as the one-leg group's `client_group_ref` (UNIQUE), so a replay reaches the same group and order rows before any send, and the `orderLinkId` comes only from the `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3 generator, never from the key (§8.3 rule 1); a replay returns the original result with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. Contract first: before this ticket's code, a contract PR aligns the `22-api-openapi.yaml` texts that still derive the `orderLinkId` from the key (the `POST /orders` description, `IdempotencyKeyRequired`, `Order.order_link_id` and the `GET /orders` example id) with §8.3 and regenerates the protocol artefacts.
- Transport selection by capability, not environment conditional: `ExchangeCapabilities.supports_ws_order_entry` chooses WS trade (live, gated off until R4) or REST (demo). No `if environment ==` outside the adapter.
- Amend (`PATCH /orders/{orderId}`) and cancel (`DELETE /orders/{orderId}`) paths, including the Bybit TP/SL re-pairing rule (amending one side of a TP/SL pair breaks OCO pairing, so the server re-sends both and records the paired amend in `order_events`), and `order_not_amendable` when terminal or with an operation in flight.
- `POST /orders/cancel-all` per-account fan-out with per-account results (`BulkAccountResult`), serialising to Bybit's 1 req/s per-account cancel-all cost.
- Implement the `B1` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B01.order.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('order', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/01_order.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_01_order.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
Rate-limit **governor** design and multi-account budgeting (E34 — T04 calls `RateBudget.acquire` with the single-account implementation from E08/E34's interface). Risk-cap evaluation logic (E39). Bracket/child sizing and the full native-SL enforcement with partial-fill awareness (E32). Sizing *modes* (% equity, risk-based) which live in the profile engine (E28) — T04 consumes `Sizer`.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Happy path is an acceptance, not a fill
  When a valid limit order is submitted
  Then the API returns 202 with the trade group and the order in state submitted
  And the response explicitly does not claim a fill

Scenario: Filters are enforced before any exchange call
  Given a price that is not a multiple of tick_size
  When submission is attempted
  Then it is rejected with tick_size_violation and no HTTP request reaches Bybit

Scenario: Entry without a stop is refused
  Given an entry intent with no stop_loss and a profile with no SL offset
  When submission is attempted
  Then it is rejected with validation_failed / native_stop_required before any exchange call

Scenario: Transport failure lands in Unknown, never in a retry
  Given the adapter raises a timeout after the request was sent
  Then the order is persisted as unknown with an event and an alert
  And no second create request is issued

Scenario: Idempotent replay
  Given the same Idempotency-Key is posted twice
  Then the second call returns the original result with Idempotency-Replayed true and creates no second order

Scenario: Amend rejection keeps the prior order live
  Given an amend is rejected by the exchange
  Then the API reports the rejection and the order's prior price and quantity are unchanged

Scenario: Order entry blocked when we cannot record it
  Given Postgres is unreachable
  Then submission returns 503 service_unavailable before any exchange call
```

## Technical notes / design
Concurrency: one `asyncio.Task` per leg; per-order keyed lock; `CV_OMS_SUBMIT_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 5000) bounds the adapter call and converts overrun into `unknown`. Config keys: `CV_OMS_SUBMIT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `CV_OMS_SL_ATTACH_DEADLINE_MS` (`T_sl`, default 3000), `CV_OMS_MAX_SUBMIT_ATTEMPTS` (bounded by the `ord_attempts` CHECK ≤10), `CV_TRADING_LIVE_ENABLED` (false until R4). Clock drift: `ClockDriftError` (10002) blocks order entry entirely and raises a distinct alert (ADR-0006 rule 6).
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B1.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
Unit: validator matrix (every filter, both directions), error-code mapping for every Bybit `retCode` in the fixture corpus, idempotency replay, capability-based transport selection, TP/SL re-pairing. Contract: request/response bodies validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml` for `/orders`, `/orders/{orderId}`, `/orders/cancel-all`. Integration (`docker-compose.test.yml` + fixture-replay mock exchange): submit → ack → partial fill → full fill; submit → business reject; submit → timeout → unknown; amend accept/reject; cancel race. Perf: backend-added overhead ≤50 ms p95 measured with the exchange mocked at zero latency. Coverage ≥90%.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B1.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
STRIDE items realised here (see E29-X01): **Spoofing** — every call authenticated, `orders:write` + `granted_accounts` scope enforced server-side before validation; **Tampering** — request body validated strictly (`additionalProperties: false`); **Repudiation** — write-ahead `order_events` with `source` and actor; **Information disclosure** — exchange `retMsg` is passed through to the user only via the audited diagnostics surface, and never includes signatures; **DoS** — `Idempotency-Key` required, per-user submit rate limit, rate-budget rejection rather than unbounded queueing; **Elevation** — environment match check makes a demo-scoped actor structurally unable to reach live. Live transport stays behind `CV_TRADING_LIVE_ENABLED=false` until E44.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI, but error codes must map to the human strings in the E29-D06 copy deck so the UI never shows a raw code alone.

## Performance notes
Budget #4: backend-added portion ≤50 ms p95 (hard, CandleViewer-controlled), end-to-end demo p95 <300 ms. Validation is O(1) against cached instrument metadata; no per-submit database read beyond the idempotency/collision lookup.

## Observability
`order_submit_seconds{transport,env}` (p99 ≤500 ms), `oms_submit_rejected_total{code}`, `oms_unknown_orders` gauge (**page if >0 for 60 s**), `oms_clock_drift_blocked_total` (alert >0), trace span `oms.submit` with child spans for validate/persist/send.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified by an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§4.2).
- [ ] Coverage: touched backend/OMS packages ≥90% line (local R3 policy for OMS/risk modules, `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4), frontend ≥80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated: `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md` / `21-database-schema.md` reflect shipped behaviour; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] Security: SAST (Bandit/Semgrep/CodeQL) + SCA clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present (mandatory — `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8, order-placement path).
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo) — never live.
- [ ] PR(s) merged through the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner; PR ≤400 LOC diff preferred.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`trading.oms_enabled`, default on for demo, off for live until R4).
- [ ] `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E29-T02 (`orderLinkId`), E29-T03 (state machine), E29-K01 (measured demo path and error-shape fixtures).

## Branch
`feat/oms-core-submit-pipeline`

title: Consume the private WS streams as the source of truth for orders, fills and positions
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B1). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. Maps pushes to events; `(ts_exec, seq)` ordering stays in bindings (MUSTNOT-04).

## Context
ADR-0006 and `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.4 are explicit: "The synchronous REST response is an acknowledgement of acceptance, not a fill confirmation — the private WS `order`/`execution` streams are the source of truth." This task wires those streams into the state machine and out to the UI over the `orders`/`positions`/`executions`/`wallet` topics, which `23-ws-protocol.md` forbids throttling or coalescing (S4).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Private-stream consumer in M14 subscribing per account to Bybit `order`, `execution.fast`, `position`, `wallet` (live `/v5/private`, demo `stream-demo`), with re-auth on reconnect and a heartbeat watchdog.
- Normalisation into the internal models of `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.1 (`Order`, `Execution`, `Position`) and dispatch as events into the B1 `order` chart (`statechart.gateway.send`) plus `apply_execution` / `apply_position` in the binding module.
- **Causal ordering** (`23-ws-protocol.md` S5): emit `executions` → `orders` → `positions` → `trade_groups` on the outbound bus so a UI never sees an effect before its cause; a reorder buffer keyed on `(ts_exec, seq)` if K01 observed exchange-side violations.
- Position projection into `positions` plus a `position_snapshots` row on `ws_push`; `wallet` balances projected for the equity figures the blotter and risk views need.
- One `execution` message may bundle several fills — each stored individually keyed by `exec_id` (`22-api-openapi.yaml` `/executions`).
- Outbound WS publication of the four private topics with account-scope intersection and silent narrowing (`23-ws-protocol.md` §private topics), `snapshot + delta` semantics, and the slow-consumer rule: if the client cannot keep up with `orders`/`executions`, close with `bye slow_consumer` / code 4429 rather than degrade them.
- Heartbeat/watchdog: on loss of the private stream, mark affected accounts `resyncing`, notify the `system` topic, and trigger a reconciliation pass (T06) on reconnect.
- Implement the `B1` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B01.order.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('order', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/01_order.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_01_order.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
The reconciliation algorithm itself (T06); WS transport/framing (E17); market-data topics; the frontend consumer (S01–S07).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: WS truth overrides the REST ack
  Given a REST ack reported state submitted
  When the private stream reports the order was already filled
  Then local state becomes filled and the ack is recorded only as an acceptance event

Scenario: Causal order is preserved
  When a fill causes an order transition and a position change
  Then subscribers receive the execution frame before the order frame and the order frame before the position frame

Scenario: Bundled fills are split
  Given one exchange execution message containing three fills
  Then three execution rows exist, each keyed by its own exec_id

Scenario: Slow consumer is disconnected, not degraded
  Given a client cannot drain the orders topic within the queue budget
  Then the server sends bye slow_consumer and closes with 4429 rather than dropping order frames

Scenario: Stream loss is visible and triggers resync
  Given the private stream drops for 30 seconds
  Then affected accounts are marked resyncing on the system topic
  And a reconciliation pass runs on reconnect
```

## Technical notes / design
One consumer task per account with its own `asyncio.TaskGroup`; module `stop()` drains with the OMS's 15 s grace window (`20-architecture.md` §Start/stop order). Backpressure: bounded queue per subscriber; `orders`/`executions` are never dropped — the connection is closed instead. Config: `CV_PRIVATE_WS_HEARTBEAT_S` (20), `CV_PRIVATE_WS_RESUB_BACKOFF` (1,2,4,8, cap 30 s, jittered).
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B1.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
Unit: normalisation of every fixture message shape; reorder buffer; bundled-fill splitting; scope intersection. Integration: fixture-replay of a recorded private session including a mid-sequence disconnect, asserting zero missed executions after backfill; slow-consumer simulation. Contract: outbound frames validated against the `orders`/`positions`/`executions` JSON Schemas in `23-ws-protocol.md` §15. Chaos (feeds Q04): 60 s stream kill, duplicate pushes, out-of-order pushes, post-terminal push. Coverage ≥90%.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B1.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
Private topics are account-scoped: the server intersects requested `exchange_account_ids` with the caller's granted scope and narrows silently; requesting only out-of-scope accounts errors with `account_scope_denied` (`23-ws-protocol.md`). Permissions required: `orders:read`, `positions:read`, `executions:read`, `accounts:read`. Cross-account leakage through the outbound fan-out is the highest-value threat here and gets a dedicated abuse test in E29-X02. Raw exchange payloads are redacted before being persisted in `order_events`.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI, but the `resyncing` / `disconnected` system states drive SCR-152 messaging designed in D03.

## Performance notes
`orders`/`executions` have `throttle_ms: 0` and must never be coalesced; `positions` may be coalesced at 10 Hz for the blotter. Backend-internal fan-out portion ≤20 ms p95 (budget #6). Private-stream processing must not be shed under load — `20-architecture.md` §shedding ladder puts OMS/private stream last and states order-related work is never shed.

## Observability
`oms_private_ws_state{account}`, `oms_private_ws_reconnects_total`, `oms_stream_event_lag_seconds{topic}`, `oms_missed_executions_total` (resolved by backfill; alert >0), `ws_slow_consumer_disconnects_total`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified by an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§4.2).
- [ ] Coverage: touched backend/OMS packages ≥90% line (local R3 policy for OMS/risk modules, `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4), frontend ≥80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated: `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md` / `21-database-schema.md` reflect shipped behaviour; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] Security: SAST (Bandit/Semgrep/CodeQL) + SCA clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present (mandatory — `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8, order-placement path).
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo) — never live.
- [ ] PR(s) merged through the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner; PR ≤400 LOC diff preferred.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`trading.oms_enabled`, default on for demo, off for live until R4).
- [ ] `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E29-T03 (the machine the events drive), E29-K01 (measured stream behaviour and fixtures). Relies on E17's WS server and E08's Bybit client.

## Branch
`feat/oms-core-private-stream`

title: Implement the reconciliation loop against order/realtime, position/list and execution/list
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B1). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. It feeds B19 events; the logic is I/O.

## Context
Reconciliation is the *only* way an `unknown` order is resolved (ADR-0006 rule 2) and the only guarantee behind US-POS-008 "the app never lies about my book". `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.5 gives the algorithm in full; this task implements it verbatim.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `Reconciler.reconcile(account, gap_from)` implementing `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.5 step by step:
  1. Fetch `GET /v5/order/realtime`, `GET /v5/position/list`, `GET /v5/execution/list` for the gap window.
  2. **Apply executions first**, sorted by `(ts_exec, seq)`, deduped by `exec_id`.
  3. Index both sides by `order_link_id` and diff:
     - present both sides → adopt exchange state, record a correction;
     - local non-terminal, absent remotely → look up `/v5/order/history`; if found, apply; else if already `unknown`, increment `unknown_passes` and after **2** passes transition to `rejected` with `UNRESOLVED_AFTER_RECONCILE`; else transition to `unknown` with reason `missing_remote`; an `untracked` row is never made `unknown`: 2 passes with no record close it as `cancelled`; an `ext-` row is looked up by `exchange_order_id`;
     - remote with no non-terminal local row → a `ReconcileAnomaly` when a terminal or another account's row holds its id, otherwise `adopt_untracked` under its normalised id (state `untracked`, displayed, never rule-managed).
  4. Positions: exchange is truth; record drift.
  5. **Safety re-check**: any open position with no exchange-side stop gets `attach_protective_sl(reason="reconcile_missing_sl")` and is recorded in `sl_repaired` (ADR-0008 / arch P4).
  6. Emit `ReconcileReport`, audit `oms.reconcile`, publish corrections on the bus so every view converges.
- Triggers: **startup**, **every private-WS reconnect**, **every 30 s**, and **on demand** from the admin screen (`POST` hook consumed by E42).
- Demo retention rule: an `order_link_id` older than 6 days on demo is closed as `rejected` with `DEMO_RETENTION_EXPIRED` (policy from T02).
- Stale-account rule (US-POS-008 scenario 3): if reconciliation fails repeatedly for **2 minutes**, the account is marked `stale`, order entry for it is disabled, and the state is published on the `system` topic for SCR-152/SCR-063.
- Rate discipline: reconciliation uses the `poll` bucket only and never starves the `critical` (protective) or `entry` buckets (`20-architecture.md` §4.3).
- Implement the `B1` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B01.order.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('order', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/01_order.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_01_order.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
The rate-limit governor (E34); the SL *attachment* mechanics and bracket awareness (E32 — T06 calls `attach_protective_sl`); admin UI (E42); chaos test authoring (Q04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Unknown resolves without resubmission
  Given an order in unknown whose orderLinkId is live at the exchange
  When reconciliation runs
  Then the order adopts the exchange state and no create request is issued

Scenario: Unresolvable order is abandoned deterministically
  Given an order in unknown that two consecutive passes cannot find in realtime or history
  Then it becomes rejected with reject_code UNRESOLVED_AFTER_RECONCILE and the abandonment is audited

Scenario: Exchange truth wins and is explained
  Given local state says the position is 0.2 and the exchange says 0.1
  Then local state is corrected to 0.1, a warning is raised, and the audit record contains both values

Scenario: Manual exchange orders are adopted, not managed
  Given an order exists at Bybit that we never created
  Then it is stored as untracked, shown in the blotter, and is never acted on by rules or algos

Scenario: A naked position is repaired
  Given an open position with no exchange-side stop-loss
  When reconciliation runs
  Then a protective stop is attached, the repair is audited, and naked_position_alerts_total increments

Scenario: Repeated failure disables entry for that account
  Given reconciliation has failed for 2 minutes on account B
  Then account B is marked stale, order entry for it is refused, and the state is published to clients
```

## Technical notes / design
`gap_from = last_seen_ts` per account, persisted so a restart does not re-fetch the world. One reconciliation task per account, serialised per account (a pass never overlaps itself). `ReconcileReport` fields: `corrected`, `resolved_from_history`, `abandoned`, `newly_unknown`, `untracked`, `anomalies`, `position_drift`, `sl_repaired`, `gap_window`. Config: `CV_OMS_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_S` (30), `CV_OMS_UNKNOWN_MAX_PASSES` (2), `CV_OMS_STALE_AFTER_S` (120).
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B1.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
Unit: each branch of the algorithm with hand-built local/remote sets; the 2-pass abandonment counter; demo-retention expiry; drift detection arithmetic. Integration (fixture-replay mock exchange): kill the process mid-submission then reconcile; 60 s stream outage with fills during the gap; duplicate acks; an exchange-side order we never created; a naked position. Contract: REST fixture shapes for `/v5/order/realtime`, `/v5/position/list`, `/v5/execution/list`, `/v5/order/history` (`03-testing-strategy.md` §4.1 `rest_*.json`). Coverage ≥90%.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B1.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
Reconciliation is the control that makes repudiation and silent divergence detectable — every correction is an audit event with before/after values (`04-security-program.md` audit requirements). Threat: a compromised or misconfigured account scope causing another account's orders to be adopted locally — the reconciler always fetches per `exchange_account_id` and asserts every returned row belongs to the requested account before applying, failing loudly otherwise. Reconciliation must never log key material; REST request signing stays in the adapter.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI; the correction and stale states it publishes are rendered by E29-S07 per the D03 design.

## Performance notes
A full pass for one account must complete in ≤2 s p95 and must fit the `poll` rate bucket; 5 accounts reconcile concurrently without exceeding per-UID budgets. The 30 s cadence bounds worst-case `unknown` residency (ADR-0006 accepted consequence).

## Observability
`oms_reconcile_seconds{account}`, `oms_reconcile_corrections_total{kind}`, `oms_unknown_orders` gauge, `oms_untracked_orders` gauge, `naked_position_alerts_total` (**page >0**), `oms_account_stale{account}`; audit event `oms.reconcile` carrying the full report.

- [ ] `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.
