title: Expose the OMS REST surface and order diagnostics
body:
## Context
The blotters (S01–S08) and every other trading epic consume the OMS through REST. `22-api-openapi.yaml` already specifies the contract; this task implements it exactly, interface-first per `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement, matching the spec byte-for-byte in request/response shape, status codes and `x-rbac`:
  - `GET /orders` (filters: accounts, symbol, `state[]`, `intent[]`, `trade_group_id`, `open_only`, `from`/`to`, cursor pagination)
  - `GET /orders/{orderId}` (`include_events`), `PATCH /orders/{orderId}` (amend), `DELETE /orders/{orderId}` (cancel — idempotent on terminal orders, returns 202 with current state)
  - `POST /orders` (single-account wrapper creating a one-leg trade group), `POST /orders/cancel-all` (per-account `BulkAccountResult`)
  - `GET /orders/{orderId}/diagnostics` — the ordered `order_events` chain plus exchange request/response pairs **with credentials and signatures redacted** and the reconciliation verdict; **audited on read**; the only place raw `retCode`/`retMsg` are exposed
  - `GET /positions` (incl. `aggregate=true` producing `AggregatePosition` rows with a per-account breakdown), `GET /positions/{positionId}`, `POST /positions/{positionId}/close`, `POST /positions/{positionId}/reverse`, `PUT /positions/{positionId}/leverage`, `POST /positions/close-all`
  - `GET /executions`, `GET /executions/closed-pnl`
- Cross-cutting: `Idempotency-Key` required on all mutating routes; `ETag`/`If-Match` on amend; RBAC permission + `granted_accounts` scope on every route; cursor pagination; strict request validation (`additionalProperties: false`).
- Contract tests generated from `22-api-openapi.yaml` wired into CI as a required check.

## Out of scope
`POST /trade-groups*` and `/trade-groups/preview` (E28/E34); `/trading/kill-switch` (E39); `/risk/*` (E39); rule and journal routes. Partial-close *business* rules beyond issuing a reduce-only order (E29-S03 covers the remainder-protection UX; E32 owns protective-quantity adjustment).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Contract conformance
  When the generated contract suite runs against the implementation
  Then every listed operation matches the OpenAPI schema for request, response and status codes with zero deviations

Scenario: Scope is enforced server-side
  Given a manager granted access only to account A
  When they request orders for account B
  Then the response is 403 account_scope_denied, no rows for B are returned by any filter combination, and an audit row is written

Scenario: Cancelling a terminal order is idempotent
  Given an order that is already filled
  When cancel is called
  Then the response is 202 with the current state rather than an error

Scenario: Diagnostics never leak secrets
  When the diagnostics endpoint is called
  Then the returned exchange request/response pairs contain no API key, no signature and no recv-window credential
  And the read itself is recorded in the audit log

Scenario: Aggregate positions never mix environments
  When positions are requested with aggregate=true across a demo and a live account
  Then the aggregate is produced per environment and never sums across them
```

## Technical notes / design
FastAPI routers in the gateway module delegating to M14 services; no business logic in the route layer. Reduce-only is forced on every close/flatten path (`/positions/{id}/close` issues a reduce-only opposite-side order and cancels the attached TP/SL of the closed portion to avoid orphan conditionals). Reverse is a single `2 × size` order in one-way mode and an explicit close+open pair in hedge mode, with the new side receiving a profile-derived native stop — rejected before sending if the profile cannot produce one (arch P4). Trailing-stop unit translation lives in the OMS (`TrailingTranslator`), never in the UI (`20-architecture.md` §9 rule 6).

## Test plan
Contract: full generated suite (required CI check). Unit: filter/pagination logic, aggregation, reduce-only forcing, hedge-mode reverse branch. Integration: each route end to end against the mock exchange incl. failure statuses 403/404/409/412/422/429/502/503. Security tests: the RBAC route×role matrix subset covering these routes (full matrix is E42/E43) asserting 403 + no state change + audit row. Coverage ≥90%.

## Security notes
Highest-risk surface in the epic. Controls: permission checks (`orders:read/write`, `positions:read/write`, `executions:read`) with `granted_accounts` scoping applied in the query layer (never post-filtered in Python); mandatory idempotency keys; `If-Match` optimistic concurrency on amend to prevent lost-update races; audited reads on diagnostics; redaction of exchange credentials; rate limiting per user on mutating routes; error bodies that never echo internal stack traces. Requires the `security` label and Security-engineer sign-off (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — API. Error codes must map to the D06 copy deck strings.

## Performance notes
`GET /orders?open_only=true` and `GET /positions` must be index-only (T01 partial indexes) and return p95 <150 ms for 1 000 orders. Mutating routes contribute to budget #4's ≤50 ms backend portion.

## Observability
Per-route latency/status histograms; `oms_api_forbidden_total{route}`; audit events `order.submitted|amended|cancelled`, `position.closed|reversed|leverage_changed`, `order.diagnostics_viewed`.

title: Stuck-order and unknown-order detection with the OMS metric and alert set
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B1). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. The detection is the chart's coarse `after:` (>=250 ms tolerant) plus `cv_machine_*` metrics from E50-T60.

## Context
ADR-0006 rule 3 is explicit: "`oms_unknown_orders > 0` for 60 s pages the operator. An unknown order is an operational incident, not a background condition." The roadmap also names **stuck-order detection** as E29 scope (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2). Detection has to be a first-class, tested feature rather than a dashboard someone might look at.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stuck-order detector scanning for, and raising a typed incident on:
  - `idempotency_state = 'in_flight'` older than `CV_OMS_INFLIGHT_STUCK_S` (default 30 s) — backed by `ix_orders_inflight`;
  - `state = 'unknown'` for more than one reconciliation cycle;
  - `state ∈ (cancel_pending, amend_pending)` for more than `CV_OMS_PENDING_STUCK_S` (default 15 s);
  - open position with `stop_loss IS NULL` (via `ix_pos_no_sl`) for more than `T_sl = 3 s`;
  - account with a failing reconciliation for >120 s (stale).
- Each detection emits a structured incident event on the bus, an audit record, and a notification usable by E40 (alerts) and E42 (system health) — this task defines the event contract, it does not build those UIs.
- The full OMS metric set from `20-architecture.md` §12 registered and documented: `order_submit_seconds{transport,env}`, `oms_unknown_orders`, `oms_untracked_orders`, `oms_state_transitions_total{from,to,source}`, `oms_reconcile_seconds`, `oms_reconcile_corrections_total{kind}`, `naked_position_alerts_total`, `oms_illegal_transitions_total`, `oms_rate_reject_total`, `bybit_rate_remaining{endpoint_group}`.
- Prometheus alerting rules + a Grafana "OMS health" dashboard as code: page on `naked_position_alerts_total > 0`, `oms_unknown_orders > 0 for 60s`, Postgres down, clock drift blocking trading (`20-architecture.md` §12 paging list).
- Structured logging: every OMS log line carries `order_link_id`, `account_id`, `environment`, `state`.
- Implement the `B1` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B01.order.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('order', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/01_order.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_01_order.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
Alert delivery channels and the notification centre (E40); the admin health screen (E42); the kill-switch (E39); the reconciliation logic itself (T06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An unknown order pages
  Given an order has been in unknown for 61 seconds
  Then oms_unknown_orders is greater than zero, the alert rule fires, and an incident event with the order_link_id is emitted

Scenario: A stuck in-flight submission is detected
  Given an order has been idempotency_state in_flight for 31 seconds
  Then a stuck-order incident is raised naming the order and its age

Scenario: A naked position is detected within the deadline
  Given an open position with no exchange-side stop-loss
  When 3 seconds elapse
  Then naked_position_alerts_total increments and a critical incident is emitted

Scenario: Alert rules are tested, not assumed
  When the alert-rule unit tests run against synthetic metric series
  Then each rule fires exactly for the intended series and not for the near-miss series
```

## Technical notes / design
Detector runs on a 5 s timer, queries are index-only over the partial indexes from T01, and each finding is deduplicated per `order_link_id` with a cool-down so a single incident does not storm the bus. Incident event schema: `{kind, severity, order_link_id?, account_id, symbol?, age_s, detected_at, detail}`. Alert rules live in the repo and are unit-tested with `promtool test rules`.
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B1.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
Unit: each detector predicate with boundary ages (just under/over threshold); dedupe cool-down; incident schema validation. Integration: force each condition against the mock exchange (kill mid-submit for in-flight; drop the stream for unknown; suppress the SL attach for naked position) and assert both the metric and the incident. `promtool` rule tests as a CI check. Coverage ≥90%.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B1.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
Incident payloads and metric labels must not carry secrets or high-cardinality user data; `order_link_id` is the only identifier included and it is opaque. Alerting endpoints are internal-only (Tailscale). Audit trail of incidents is append-only.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI in this ticket; the health surface is E42.

## Performance notes
The detector must add <1% to steady-state CPU and must not compete with the submit path for database connections — it uses a dedicated low-priority pool.

## Observability
This ticket *is* the observability deliverable for E29; the Grafana dashboard JSON and alert rules are committed alongside the code (`ADR-0014-observability.md`).

title: Build the SCR-063 positions tab with cross-account rows, grouping and liq-proximity warnings
body:
## Context
US-POS-001 (Must) - "I want all positions across symbols and accounts in one panel, so that I see my whole book." This is the first user-visible surface of the OMS and the screen the owner watches while money is at risk. Screen spec: `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-063 (tabbed panel: Positions / Working orders / Fills / Trade groups / Algos). This story delivers the panel shell plus the **Positions** tab and the US-POS-006 account/group filtering the shell owns; the other tabs are E29-S02/S04, and the Trade-groups and Algos tabs are stubs owned by E34/E33.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: **US-POS-001**, **US-POS-006**, and the display half of **US-POS-007** (one-way vs hedge rows keyed by `position_idx`, CMP-129 PositionModeToggle rendered read-only here; switching the mode is E27's account config).
- Screen **SCR-063** panel shell with its five tabs, tab state persisted in the workspace layout.
- Columns per the SCR-063 wireframe: account, symbol, side (as text, never colour alone), qty, entry, mark, uPnL, R, rPnL today, leverage, margin mode, liq price; TOTAL row associated via `scope`.
- Components: **CMP-114** PositionsGrid (extends **CMP-049** Table), **CMP-116** PnLBadge, **CMP-105** AccountMultiSelect, **CMP-055** FilterBar, **CMP-056** ColumnPicker, **CMP-057** SplitButton (row actions), **CMP-129** PositionModeToggle.
- Data: WS topic `positions` (snapshot + delta, 100 ms throttle) with `GET /api/v1/positions` for the initial load and as the reconciliation fallback.
- Group-by account / symbol / trade group / manager, with aggregate rows expanding to per-account rows.
- Liq-proximity warning: escalating row treatment with an `!` glyph **and** the text "within N% of liquidation".
- States: loading / empty ("No open positions") / reconciling / desync banner / lockout (actions disabled with reasons) / viewer read-only.
- CSV export of the current view (`grid.exported` audit event).

## Out of scope
Working-orders tab (E29-S02), fills tab (E29-S04), mutating row actions such as partial close (E29-S03), position detail drawer (E29-S08), reconciliation banner semantics (E29-S07 defines them; this story renders the state), trade-group and algo tabs (E34/E33), chart execution marks (E29-S05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Rows render the whole book
  Given open positions exist on accounts Main and sub_001
  When the positions tab loads
  Then each row shows account, symbol, side as text, qty, entry, mark, uPnL, rPnL today, leverage, margin mode and liquidation price
  And a TOTAL row aggregates size and PnL

Scenario: Grouping by trade group
  When I group by trade group
  Then group rows aggregate size and PnL and expand to per-account rows

Scenario: Liquidation proximity is not colour-only
  Given the mark price is within the configured distance of the liquidation price
  Then the row shows an "!" glyph and the text "within 1.4% of liquidation" in addition to any colour

Scenario: Manager scope is enforced server-side
  Given I am signed in as a manager granted only account B
  When I craft a request filtering to account A
  Then the API returns only account B rows and the out-of-scope request is refused and audited

Scenario: Live update latency
  When a position event arrives on the WS positions topic
  Then the row updates within 200 ms

Scenario: Empty state
  Given no open positions exist
  Then an explicit empty state is shown and no error is rendered
```

## Technical notes / design
Store: a normalised positions atom keyed `(exchange_account_id, symbol, position_idx)` fed by the `positions` WS topic; frames older than the held `updated_at_ms` are discarded (`23-ws-protocol.md` section 15 late-frame rule). Rendering is virtualised over CMP-049; updates are coalesced into a 10 Hz render tick so a burst of position pushes cannot thrash the frame budget. Money is rendered from `Decimal`-safe strings and never parsed into a JS `number` before display rounding. `R` is derived from the position's stop distance when a native SL exists, otherwise rendered as "-". Filter chips are removable and reflected in the layout state so a workspace reload restores them.

## Test plan
Unit: row mapping, grouping/aggregation, liq-proximity thresholding, late-frame discard, filter-chip reducer. Contract: WS `positions` payload validated against `cv://ws/v1/positions.schema.json` in CI. Integration: MSW-backed `GET /api/v1/positions` plus a scripted WS fixture stream. E2E (Playwright, web + Electron): load with 3 accounts, group by account and by trade group, filter and clear, and assert manager scoping using a manager session. Perf: 500-row render benchmark at 60 fps. Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Threat: cross-account information disclosure (a manager seeing the owner's book). Control: the REST API and the WS subscription narrow to `granted_accounts` server-side (`23-ws-protocol.md` sections 6.2/6.3); the client never filters for security purposes. Threat: treating the exported CSV as an audit substitute - the export is an analytics convenience while `order_events`/`audit_log` remain the record. Data classification: financial/restricted. No key material is rendered on this screen.

## Accessibility notes
Real table semantics; sortable headers expose `aria-sort`; row actions are reachable through a per-row menu button, never hover-only; the totals row is associated via `scope`; liq-proximity is glyph plus text, never colour alone; the virtualised list keeps a stable roving-tabindex focus model and announces position in the set; column picker and filter bar are fully keyboard operable (`05-accessibility-standard.md` section 6.1 windowed-grid rules).

## Performance notes
SCR-063 budget: virtualised, **500 rows at 60 fps**, position updates coalesced at 10 Hz. The grid holds a rolling snapshot rather than history, keeping its contribution inside the <=1.5 GB workspace ceiling (budget #7).

title: Build the SCR-063 working-orders tab with inline amend, cancel and conditional-order sections
body:
## Context
US-POS-002 (Must) - all working orders listed with their state so they can be managed centrally - plus the blotter half of **US-ORD-009** (cancel an order from the grid) and **US-ORD-010** (the flatten / cancel-all entry point, CMP-123). The state vocabulary is `24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.2 and the WS `OrderUpdate` enum (`new, pending_submit, submitted, accepted, partially_filled, filled, pending_cancel, cancelled, pending_amend, rejected, expired, untracked`). Showing a wrong order state is a safety problem, so pending states must be visually distinct from acknowledged ones - transition rule S2 says an amend rejection leaves the prior order live, and a user who believes a stop moved when it did not is in danger.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: **US-POS-002**, plus the blotter portion of **US-ORD-009** and **US-ORD-010**.
- Working-orders tab on **SCR-063** using **CMP-115** OrderRow inside CMP-114/CMP-049, plus **CMP-123** FlattenAllButton wired to `POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all` and `POST /api/v1/positions/close-all`.
- Columns: account, symbol, side, type, qty, filled qty, price, trigger price and source, TIF, flags (reduce-only, post-only, close-on-trigger), age, parent algo or bracket, state.
- A distinct **untriggered conditional orders** section with the trigger condition spelled out in words.
- Inline amend of price/quantity via `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, rendered as **pending** until the WS `orders` frame with `change: "amend"` confirms; on rejection the prior values are restored and the exchange `retMsg` is shown verbatim.
- Row cancel via `DELETE /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`; multi-select cancel; cancel-all behind the confirm policy with a per-order partial-failure list.
- `untracked` orders rendered in their own visual class with the copy "placed outside CandleViewer - displayed, not managed" (state machine rule S9).

## Out of scope
Chart and DOM cancel gestures (E31), bracket-child visualisation beyond a parent reference (E32), the algo monitor (E33), the kill-switch modal SCR-072 (E39), order-ticket amend UX (E30).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Rows carry the full order vocabulary
  Then each order row shows account, symbol, side, type, quantity, filled quantity, price, trigger, TIF, flags, age and its parent algorithm or bracket

Scenario: Optimistic amend is clearly pending
  When I amend a price inline
  Then the row enters a visibly pending state labelled "amend pending"
  And it becomes confirmed only when the WS orders frame with change "amend" arrives

Scenario: Amend rejection leaves the order untouched
  Given the exchange rejects the amend
  Then the row returns to its previous values, the exchange message is shown verbatim, and the row is marked "amend rejected - original order still live"

Scenario: Conditional orders are separated
  Then untriggered conditional orders appear in a distinct section stating trigger price, trigger source and direction in words

Scenario: Cancel that lost the race
  Given the order filled before the cancel arrived
  Then the error is translated to "already filled" and the row moves to the filled state rather than showing a raw exchange error

Scenario: Cancel-all partial failure
  Given cancel-all succeeds on 3 of 5 accounts
  Then a per-account result list is shown with the failure reason for each failing account and nothing is silently dropped

Scenario: Virtualised at scale
  Given 1 000 working orders
  Then the grid renders, sorts and filters without dropping below the frame budget and every control stays keyboard reachable
```

## Technical notes / design
The `orders` WS topic is never throttled or coalesced (`23-ws-protocol.md` section 6.2): the client applies every frame, and if it cannot keep up the server closes the socket with 4429 - so the apply path must be O(1) per frame against a keyed map rather than a list scan. Optimistic state lives in a separate `pendingMutations` map keyed by `order_link_id` and is additive to server state rather than replacing it, which is what makes rule S2 renderable. `Idempotency-Key` is required on cancel-all and close-all (`22-api-openapi.yaml` `x-idempotency: required`); the client generates one UUIDv4 per user gesture and reuses it across retries of that gesture.

## Test plan
Unit: state-to-label mapping for all twelve order states, pending-mutation overlay, partial-failure reducer, age formatter. Contract: WS `orders` frames against `cv://ws/v1/orders.schema.json`; amend/cancel against the OpenAPI schema. Integration: fixture stream producing amend-ack, amend-reject, cancel-lost-race and untracked-adoption sequences. E2E: inline amend happy path and rejection path; cancel-all with two failing accounts asserting the per-account list. Perf: 1 000-row virtualisation benchmark. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
`orders:write` with `granted_accounts` scope is enforced server-side on every amend and cancel; the UI hides controls it may not use, but the API is the enforcement point (abuse case covered by E29-X02). Cancel-all has a high blast radius: it requires the confirm policy, carries an idempotency key, and emits an `order.cancelled` audit row per order. Exchange `retMsg` strings are rendered as text, never as HTML - exchange-controlled strings are untrusted input.

## Accessibility notes
Pending and rejected states are conveyed by icon plus text, never colour alone (CMP-115 contract); state changes are announced in a polite live region with debouncing so a burst does not flood the screen reader; cancel-all is keyboard-operable with a real confirm dialog and never a mouse-hold-only gate (CMP-123 contract); sortable headers expose `aria-sort`; active filters are removable chips with text labels.

## Performance notes
Virtualised for >=1 000 rows; `orders` frames are applied unthrottled with a target of <=2 ms scripting per frame apply, measured in the E29-Q03 harness against the SCR-063 500-row/60 fps budget.

## Observability
Analytics `order.amend_attempted`, `order.cancel_attempted`, `blotter.cancel_all_invoked`; audit rows (`order.amended`, `order.cancelled`) are emitted server-side. Client metric `pending_mutation_age_seconds` catches acknowledgements that never arrive.

title: Implement partial close with reduce-only sizing and protective-order quantity adjustment
body:
## Context
US-POS-003 (Must) - close part of a position by quantity or percentage. This is simultaneously a backend concern (reduce-only correctness, lot rounding, keeping the native stop sized to what remains) and a UI concern (the `[Close 25%][Close 50%][Close]` row actions in SCR-063). Getting it wrong either reverses a position accidentally or leaves a protective stop sized for a position that no longer exists - both are safety incidents, which is why this is a separate story from the read-only blotter work.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Story: **US-POS-003**; endpoint `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/close` (accepting `qty` or `percent`), consumed by the SCR-063 row actions via **CMP-057** SplitButton.
- Backend: quantity resolution (percent -> base qty -> floor to `lotSizeFilter.qtyStep` read from `instruments`), **always** `reduceOnly: true`, `positionIdx` carried through for hedge mode, and order `purpose="flatten"` so the request draws from the protective rate-budget reserve (`24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.7).
- Protective-order resizing: after the reducing fill, remaining native SL/TP quantities are rewritten to the remaining position size in a single `POST /v5/position/trading-stop` call carrying **both** TP and SL (the one-sided-modification caveat in section 8.9).
- Dust guard: if rounding would leave a remainder below `minOrderQty`, the API returns `422 dust_remainder` with the computed remainder and the UI offers "close the full position instead".
- UI: confirmation per the confirm policy, a pending state until the execution arrives, and a single reported operation rather than two.

## Out of scope
Flatten-all and the panic button (E39 owns the kill-switch; cancel-all plumbing is E29-S02), reverse (E31/E32), bracket child re-sizing on partial entry fills (E32), TP-ladder editing on SCR-064 (E32).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Percentage close
  Given a long position of 0.250 BTC
  When I choose 50%
  Then a reduce-only order for 0.125 rounded to the lot size is submitted with purpose "flatten"

Scenario: Protective quantities follow the remainder
  Given the partial close fills
  Then the native stop-loss and take-profit quantities are rewritten to the remaining size in one trading-stop call sending both sides
  And the position is never left with a protective order sized larger than the position

Scenario: Rounding leaves dust
  Given closing 50% would leave a remainder below the symbol minimum order quantity
  Then the request is rejected with 422 dust_remainder before any exchange call and the UI offers a full close

Scenario: Never reverses
  Given the position shrank between the request and the send
  Then the reduce-only flag causes the exchange to cap or reject the order and no opposite-side position is opened

Scenario: Hedge mode
  Given the account is in hedge mode with a long and a short on the same symbol
  Then the close applies only to the requested position_idx and the opposite side is untouched
```

## Technical notes / design
Resolution order: `qty = floor(position.size * percent / qty_step) * qty_step`; reject with `422 qty_below_minimum` when `qty <= 0`, and with `422 dust_remainder` when `position.size - qty` falls in `(0, minOrderQty)`. The close order is an ordinary OMS submission (E29-T04) with `reduce_only=True`, `close_on_trigger=False`, `purpose="flatten"`, `origin="blotter"`. The protective resize runs from the execution handler rather than optimistically, and is retried three times with 250 ms backoff before raising a `critical` over-sized-stop alert. `REDUCE_ONLY_VIOLATION` (Bybit 110017) re-derives the true position and refreshes the blotter instead of surfacing a raw exchange error.

## Test plan
Unit: percent-to-qty rounding table (33%, one-lot positions, `qty_step` 0.001 and 1), dust detection, hedge `position_idx` routing, protective-resize payload asserting both sides are present. Integration: fixture-replay covering partial close -> fill -> resize -> assert `positions.stop_loss` quantity; a race fixture in which the position shrinks mid-flight and returns 110017. Chaos (feeds E29-Q04): kill the backend between the close fill and the protective resize, restart, and assert the resize completes on recovery. Coverage >=90% backend.

## Security notes
An order-placement path, therefore `security`-labelled by default (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8). Threats: elevation (closing a position on an account outside the caller's grant), mitigated by `positions:write` plus `granted_accounts`; tampering (a client-supplied qty larger than the position), mitigated because the server re-derives from exchange-truth position state and never trusts the client's size; repudiation, mitigated by a `position.closed` audit row recording requested versus resolved quantity. An over-sized protective order after a partial close is treated as a safety defect, not a cosmetic one.

## Accessibility notes
Row actions live in a per-row menu with text labels ("Close 25%"), never icon-only; the confirmation dialog states resolved quantity, any rounding note ("Rounded to 0.001") and the resulting remaining size in text; the pending state is announced politely; no action depends on hover or a pointer hold.

## Performance notes
The close submission rides budget #4 (submit->ack p95 <300 ms on demo, backend-added <=50 ms). The protective resize must complete inside the same 2 s deadline the native-SL invariant uses (`24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.8 rule 2).

## Observability

title: Build the fills tab and the SCR-078 executions detail drawer
body:
## Context
Fills are the only exchange-truth record of what actually happened, and both the journal (E41) and the position detail (E29-S08) derive from them. US-POS-005 and US-POS-009 both need a per-fill view, and `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-078 specifies it: time, price, qty, fee, fee currency, liquidity flag, order id, exec id, trade group, the rule that caused it and a journal link.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: the fills half of **US-POS-005** and **US-POS-009**; screen **SCR-078** (drawer) plus the Fills tab inside SCR-063.
- Components: **CMP-049** Table, **CMP-036** KeyValueRow, **CMP-046** Drawer, **CMP-099** PrintExportBar, **CMP-116** PnLBadge.
- Data: WS topic `executions` (never throttled) plus `GET /api/v1/executions` with cursor pagination for history.
- Aggregation: average fill price with the maker/taker split; slippage versus the intended price wherever an intent price exists; grouping by account for fanned-out orders.
- CSV export (`execution.exported` analytics); empty state; virtualised list coalesced to 5 Hz.

## Out of scope
Chart execution marks (E29-S05), closed-position PnL rollup (E29-S06), journal linkage beyond a deep link (E41), fan-out grouping semantics (E34 defines the group model; this renders it).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Per-fill detail
  Then each fill row shows time, price, quantity, fee with its currency, maker/taker flag, order id and exec id

Scenario: Aggregate and slippage
  Given an order filled in 4 executions against an intended limit price
  Then an average fill price, the maker/taker split and slippage versus the intended price are shown

Scenario: No double counting
  Given the same exec_id arrives on the WS stream and again through REST backfill
  Then it appears exactly once in the list and once in the aggregate

Scenario: Volume
  Given a 1 000-fill session
  Then the list renders without exceeding 4 ms scripting per frame and stays keyboard navigable

Scenario: Empty state
  Given no fills in the selected window
  Then an explicit empty state naming the active filter is shown
```

## Technical notes / design
Deduplication is keyed on `exec_id` client-side as well as server-side, because the backfill/stream overlap is normal rather than exceptional. Fee sign and currency are always rendered together. Slippage appears only when an intent price exists (limit orders and algo children); for market orders the column reads "-" rather than a misleading zero. The list is virtualised and coalesced at 5 Hz (the SCR-078 performance note) while the underlying `executions` topic itself stays unthrottled.

## Test plan
Unit: dedupe by `exec_id`, average-price and maker/taker aggregation, slippage computation and its absence for market orders, fee formatting. Contract: WS `executions` payload against `cv://ws/v1/executions.schema.json`. Integration: a fixture with overlapping WS and REST backfill. E2E: open the drawer from an order row, export CSV, assert the row count. Perf: 1 000-fill render benchmark asserting <=4 ms scripting per frame. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
Executions are immutable exchange records, so the UI must never offer an edit affordance. Cross-account scoping is server-side (`executions:read` plus `granted_accounts`). Exported CSV is an analytics artefact and is watermarked with the account scope and generation time so it is not mistaken for the audit trail.

## Accessibility notes
Table semantics; fees and funding shown with explicit sign and currency in text; maker/taker rendered as text rather than colour; the drawer has a heading naming order and account, traps focus, and returns focus to the invoking row on close.

## Performance notes
Virtualised and coalesced to 5 Hz; a 1 000-fill session renders without exceeding 4 ms scripting per frame (SCR-078 budget).

## Observability
`execution.detail_viewed` and `execution.exported` (analytics). Client metric `exec_dedupe_hits_total` - a non-zero value is expected, but a spike indicates backfill misconfiguration.

title: Render execution marks on the chart from the execution stream with clustering
body:
## Context
US-POS-005 (Must) - "I want fills marked on the chart, so that I see where I actually traded." The NFR is the important part: **marks come from the execution stream, never from optimistic order state**, so a mark on the chart is always something that really happened. The marks are an overlay layer in the custom WebGL engine (SCR-030), so they must obey the engine's frame-budget shedding ladder instead of being drawn as DOM elements on top of the canvas.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Story: **US-POS-005**; screens SCR-030 (chart panel) and SCR-078 (the detail it links to).
- An `executions` overlay layer in the chart engine renderer: one mark per fill at `(exec_ts, exec_price)`, glyph by side, size scaled by quantity within a bounded range.
- Clustering: fills within a configurable pixel radius collapse into a cluster glyph with a count badge that expands on hover **and** on keyboard focus.
- Tooltip / focus card: side, quantity, price, account, fee, maker/taker, order link id, and a deep link into SCR-078.
- A toggle in the chart trading overlay settings (SCR-040); when disabled the marks hide but stay available in the position detail (E29-S08).
- Account/group filter inherited from the workspace so a fanned-out trade shows only the selected accounts' marks.

## Out of scope
Order and position lines and their drag interactions (E31), the SCR-040 settings screen itself (E31), bracket visualisation (E32), replay-time marks (E26/E38).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Marks reflect reality only
  Given an order is submitted but not yet filled
  Then no mark appears on the chart
  And a mark appears only when the execution arrives on the executions stream

Scenario: Clustering at density
  Given 40 executions inside one bar's pixel width
  Then they render as a cluster glyph with a count badge that expands on hover or keyboard focus

Scenario: Toggle
  When I disable execution marks in the chart trading overlay settings
  Then no marks are drawn and the fills remain visible in the position detail view

Scenario: Frame budget
  Given 5 000 execution marks in the visible range
  Then the pane holds p95 frame time <=16.6 ms, shedding mark detail before it sheds price data
```

## Technical notes / design
Marks live in their own instanced draw call backed by a GPU buffer of `(x, y, side, qtyBucket)` so adding a fill is a buffer append rather than a scene rebuild (`26-chart-engine-design.md` layer model). Clustering is computed in screen space on the CPU once per viewport change - not per frame - and memoised by `(rangeStart, rangeEnd, pxPerBar)`. The overlay registers at a shedding tier below price and bar geometry so the frame-budget ladder drops mark detail first. Keyboard access uses the chart's existing overlay focus ring: marks join the focusable-object list in time order.

## Test plan
Unit: clustering algorithm (boundary radii, stable cluster identity across small pans), quantity-to-size bucketing, exclusion of optimistic state. Visual regression at three zoom levels. E2E: place a demo order, wait for the fill, assert a mark appears at the fill price and that its focus card contents are correct. Perf: 5 000-mark benchmark against budget #1 recorded in the engine bench suite. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
The focus card shows account labels, so it must respect the caller's account scope - a manager must not be able to infer the existence of another account's fills from marks. No key or signature material is exposed. Deep links carry `order_link_id`, which is a correlation id rather than a secret, and the target screen re-authorises.

## Accessibility notes
Every mark is reachable through the chart's keyboard object navigation with an announced description ("Buy 0.1 at 63,980, Main, maker"); clusters announce their count and expand on focus rather than only on hover; marks are distinguishable by glyph shape as well as colour; the SCR-045 chart data-table alternative lists the executions in the visible range as rows.

## Performance notes
Budget #1: p95 frame time <=16.6 ms on the focused pane with 5 000 marks enabled; the overlay participates in the shedding ladder. Mark buffer memory is bounded by the visible range plus a prefetch margin.

## Observability
`chart_overlay_marks_rendered` gauge and `chart_overlay_shed_events_total{layer="executions"}` so shedding is visible rather than silent.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified by an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§4.2).
- [ ] Coverage: touched backend/OMS packages ≥90% line (local R3 policy for OMS/risk modules, `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4), frontend ≥80%; CI coverage gate green.

## Dependencies

title: Ship closed positions and today's realised PnL with the configured day boundary
body:
## Context
US-POS-009 (Must) - today's closed positions and realised PnL. Two traps make this a story rather than a column: "today" must use **the same day boundary as the daily-loss limit** (E39) or the risk lockout and the PnL display will disagree; and fee data arrives late, so a freshly closed row must be explicitly provisional rather than quietly wrong. The NFR requires realised PnL to match Bybit's own figures within rounding tolerance, which means reconciling against `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl` rather than only summing local fills.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Story: **US-POS-009**; screens SCR-063 (closed-positions view) and SCR-078; data via `GET /api/v1/executions/closed-pnl` (mirroring Bybit `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl`).
- Rows: entry, exit, quantity, gross PnL, fees, funding, net PnL, account, symbol, side, duration.
- Day boundary read from the same configuration key the daily-loss cap uses (`risk.day_boundary_utc_offset`, owned by E39) - one source, never a second constant.
- Provisional state: rows whose fee or funding data has not settled are marked "provisional" in text and update in place once settled.
- Reconciliation badge: when locally computed net PnL differs from the exchange's `closedPnl` beyond the rounding tolerance, the row is flagged and the divergence is audited.
- Per-account and aggregated totals consistent with the positions-tab totals.

## Out of scope
Full journal analytics - equity curve, R-multiple distribution, MAE/MFE analysis, tags (E41); per-trade-group PnL rollup (E34); risk-lockout behaviour itself (E39); Parquet export (E41).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Closed today
  Then a list shows each closed position with entry, exit, quantity, gross PnL, fees, funding and net PnL

Scenario: Day boundary is shared
  Given the configured day boundary is 00:00 UTC+3
  Then "today" in this view starts at exactly the same instant the daily-loss limit resets
  And a contract test asserts both read the same configuration key

Scenario: Fees pending
  Given a position closed seconds ago whose fee data has not arrived
  Then the row shows its PnL as provisional in text and updates in place once fees settle

Scenario: Divergence from the exchange
  Given local net PnL differs from GET /v5/position/closed-pnl beyond the rounding tolerance
  Then the row is flagged, the exchange figure is displayed as authoritative, and the divergence is audited with both values
```

## Technical notes / design
Local net PnL is composed from `executions` (`closed_pnl` on reducing fills, minus `exec_fee`, plus rows with `exec_type='Funding'`) using `Decimal` arithmetic. The exchange figure is fetched per closed position and compared with a relative tolerance (`oms.closed_pnl_tolerance_rel`, default 1e-8). The comparison runs server-side so the flag is a data property rather than a rendering artefact. Config keys: `risk.day_boundary_utc_offset`, `oms.closed_pnl_tolerance_rel`.

## Test plan
Unit: PnL composition across gross/fee/funding, tolerance comparison, provisional-to-settled transition, day-boundary bucketing across the configured offset including the boundary minute. Contract: `GET /api/v1/executions/closed-pnl` against the OpenAPI schema, plus a shared-config test asserting E39's cap and this view resolve the same key. Integration: fixture with late-arriving fee rows. E2E: close a demo position and assert the row appears provisional then settles. Coverage >=85% backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Financial data, scoped server-side (`positions:read`, `executions:read`). A divergence flag is security-relevant in the repudiation sense, so it is audited with both values and a disputed figure can be reconstructed. No client-side recomputation is trusted for the audit record.

## Accessibility notes
PnL values carry a text sign and currency alongside colour (CMP-116 PnLBadge contract); "provisional" is a text label rather than a faded style; the divergence flag is an icon plus text with an accessible description naming both figures; the totals row is associated via `scope`.

## Performance notes
The closed-PnL fetch is a `background`-priority request in the rate budget (`24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.7) so it can never starve order traffic. The view paginates rather than loading unbounded history.

## Observability
`oms_closed_pnl_divergence_total{account}` (warning alert on a sustained non-zero rate), `oms_closed_pnl_fetch_seconds`. Audit: `pnl.divergence_detected` with local and exchange values.

title: Ship the reconciliation UX: desync banner, stale-account lockout and the while-you-were-away report
body:
## Context
US-POS-008 (Must) - "I want continuous reconciliation between local state and Bybit, so that the app never lies about my book." E29-T06 builds the reconciliation loop; this story makes its results legible and safe: the SCR-152 reconnecting/desync treatment, the per-account stale lockout that disables order entry, and the explicit "while you were offline: 1 order filled, 1 stop moved by a rule" report SCR-152 specifies. Without it, a correct backend still leaves the user acting on a screen they cannot trust.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Story: **US-POS-008** (UI half; the algorithm is E29-T06); screens **SCR-152** (disconnected / reconnecting / gap-filling / restored variants) and the SCR-063 "reconciling" and "desync warning" states.
- Components: **CMP-028** Callout/Banner, **CMP-035** Countdown, **CMP-076** ConnectionStatus, **CMP-077** ReconnectOverlay, **CMP-078** StaleDataShade.
- Banner states with distinct copy: connected / reconnecting (attempt N, next in M s) / gap-filling / reconciling / desync ("Position data is being verified - actions temporarily limited") / account-stale (order entry disabled for the named accounts).
- The reassurance line "Your exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected" rendered **only when it is true**, i.e. when the native-SL invariant check passed for every open position on the affected accounts.
- A "while you were away" summary built from the `ReconcileReport` (`corrected`, `resolved_from_history`, `newly_unknown`, `untracked`, `position_drift`, `sl_repaired`), each entry deep-linking to the affected row.
- Hard-disabling of trading controls while private feeds are down, with refused attempts recorded as `order.blocked_offline`.
- Per-panel stale shading showing each panel's last-good timestamp.

## Out of scope
The reconciliation algorithm, its metrics and its alerts (E29-T06/T08); the kill-switch (E39); degraded-mode variants for recorder, rule engine or GPU fallback (SCR-153, other epics); the admin System health -> OMS screen (E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reconnect with a correction
  Given the private WS was down for 60 seconds and one order filled while offline
  When the connection is restored and reconciliation completes
  Then a "while you were away" summary lists the fill with a link to the affected row
  And the blotter shows the corrected state within 30 seconds of reconnect

Scenario: Trading is blocked while blind
  Given private feeds are down
  Then every trading control is disabled with the reason shown in text
  And an attempted submission is refused client-side and recorded as order.blocked_offline

Scenario: Repeated reconciliation failure
  Given REST reconciliation fails repeatedly for 2 minutes for account A
  Then account A is marked stale, its rows are shaded with their last-good timestamp, and order entry for it is disabled while other accounts remain usable

Scenario: The reassurance must be true
  Given an open position was found without a native stop-loss during reconciliation
  Then the "your exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected" line is not shown
  And the repaired-stop entry appears in the summary instead

Scenario: The overlay never hides the book
  Then the reconnect overlay never fully obscures the positions grid
```

## Technical notes / design
The banner is driven by one `connectionState` machine (`connected -> reconnecting -> gap_filling -> reconciling -> {connected, degraded_stale}`) fed by the WS client and by `system` / `ReconcileReport` frames, rather than by ad-hoc booleans scattered through panels. The backoff display mirrors the client's actual schedule (1, 2, 4, 8 s capped at 30 s, jittered). The stale flag is per exchange account, so one impaired account does not disable the whole app. The summary is built from the server's `ReconcileReport` payload so the client never infers corrections by diffing its own cache.

## Test plan
Unit: connection-state machine transitions including flapping; summary builder for each `ReconcileReport` field; the truth-gate on the reassurance line. Integration: scripted WS drop and restore with a report containing corrections, untracked adoptions and an `sl_repaired` entry. E2E/chaos (feeds E29-Q04): kill the WS mid-session, assert controls disable, restore, assert the summary and the corrected rows. A11y: axe plus a screen-reader pass on the banner's single-announcement behaviour. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
This is a safety surface: showing "connected", or the stop-loss reassurance, when it is not true is a security-relevant misrepresentation (integrity/repudiation), so the reassurance line is gated on the invariant check rather than on connection state alone. Client-side disabling is UX only - the server independently refuses orders from stale accounts, asserted in E29-X02. `order.blocked_offline` is recorded for forensic reconstruction.

## Accessibility notes
`role="alert"` fires once on entering a state and the banner then persists as a static region - the countdown is **not** announced on every tick (SCR-152 a11y rule); disabled controls expose `aria-disabled` with a programmatically associated reason; stale panels carry a visible, readable last-good timestamp; the summary is a keyboard-navigable list of plain sentences, each item linking to its row.

## Performance notes
Target time-to-usable after a 30 s outage is <=5 s (SCR-152): subscriptions restore in priority order - private account state first, then the focused panel, then the rest - and a gap-fill request closes the missed window.

## Observability
Analytics and incident events `ws.disconnected{reason,subscriptions}`, `ws.reconnect_attempt{attempt}`, `ws.reconnected{outageMs,gapFilled}`, `order.blocked_offline`. Client gauge `account_stale{account}` mirrored to the admin health screen.

## Definition of Done

title: Build the position detail view assembled from OMS state and executions
body:
## Context
US-POS-004 (Should) - a detail view per position showing entry executions, fees, funding, MAE/MFE so far, attached protective orders, controlling rules and the journal entry. Its NFR is the design constraint: the detail is "assembled from the journal and OMS state, not recomputed ad hoc" - otherwise the drawer becomes a fourth opinion about the book.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Story: **US-POS-004**, rendered as a drawer from a SCR-063 row, reusing SCR-078's fill list and linking to SCR-064 (the SL/TP editor owned by E32) and SCR-079 (the account drawer, E27).
- Components: **CMP-036** KeyValueRow, **CMP-046** Drawer, **CMP-049** Table, **CMP-116** PnLBadge.
- Data: `GET /api/v1/positions/{positionId}` plus the executions already in the store; MAE/MFE so far computed server-side from `position_snapshots`.
- Sections: identity (account, symbol, side, position_idx, leverage, margin mode), entry executions, fees and funding paid, MAE/MFE, attached protective orders with their native-versus-engine-managed status, controlling rule ids (rule detail is E35) and the journal link (E41, a disabled link until E41 ships).
- A "show on chart" action navigating the chart to the entry time with this position's executions highlighted.
- Externally-modified notice: when the position was changed outside the app, a reconciliation notice explains the difference and when it was detected.

## Out of scope
Editing anything (SL/TP editing is SCR-064 in E32), journal note authoring (E41), rule inspection (E35), MAE/MFE analytics history and distributions (E41).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Detail contents
  Then entry executions, fees paid, funding paid, MAE/MFE so far, attached protective orders, controlling rule ids and the journal link are shown

Scenario: Jump to chart
  When I choose "show on chart"
  Then the chart navigates to the entry time and this position's executions are highlighted

Scenario: Externally modified
  Given the position was changed outside CandleViewer and reconciliation detected it
  Then a notice explains what differed and when it was detected

Scenario: No ad-hoc recomputation
  Then every figure shown matches the server-side aggregation exactly, asserted by a contract test comparing the drawer payload with the positions and executions endpoints
```

## Technical notes / design
The drawer fetches one aggregate payload; it does not assemble numbers from three stores. MAE/MFE so far is derived server-side from `position_snapshots` (`reason in ('ws_push','minute_tick')`) bounded to the position's lifetime. Protective orders are listed with their `purpose` (`stop_loss` / `take_profit`) and a native-versus-engine-managed badge sourced from `orders.intent` plus the position's `stop_loss` field, so an engine-managed trail is never mistaken for exchange-side protection.

## Test plan
Unit: payload-to-section mapping, native-versus-engine badge logic, external-modification notice rendering. Contract: the aggregate payload against the OpenAPI schema and against the individual endpoints (the "no ad-hoc recomputation" scenario). E2E: open from a row, jump to chart, assert the chart range and the highlighted marks. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
Account-scoped read (`positions:read`). The drawer surfaces rule ids and order link ids - correlation identifiers rather than secrets - and never key material or exchange signatures. The external-modification notice is sourced from audited reconciliation output, so it cannot be spoofed by client state.

## Accessibility notes
The drawer has a heading naming account, symbol and side; sections are a description list; the native-versus-engine badge is text; "show on chart" moves focus to the chart pane and announces the navigation; the drawer traps focus and restores it to the originating row on close.

## Performance notes
Opens from cached state in <=100 ms and refreshes in place (the SCR-079 drawer budget applied here).

## Observability
`position.detail_viewed` (analytics) with `{has_external_modification}` so the frequency of external modification is trackable.

title: Write the black-box test plan and Bybit fixtures for the OMS and its blotters
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature **before** code, and `30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4 names the integration fixture set R3 must cover: partial fills, rejections, `10018` rate-limit, WS disconnect mid-bracket, exchange 5xx and clock skew. E29 is the epic those fixtures serve first, so the fixtures are built here and reused by E30-E34, E38 and E45. Writing this before E29-T03/T04 land also validates the state machine's observability: if a state transition cannot be black-box observed, the ticket says so and a diagnostic is added.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A black-box test plan in `docs/qa/e29-oms-test-plan.md` covering every E29 story (S01-S08) and the externally observable behaviour of T03-T08, with one section per user story id (US-POS-001..009, US-ORD-009/010 blotter halves).
- Exploratory charters (time-boxed, session-based): "act on a stale blotter", "amend during a partial fill", "cancel exactly at fill", "manager scope probing", "reconnect storm while a partial close is in flight".
- Recorded Bybit **demo** fixtures under `packages/fixtures/oms/`: `rest_order_realtime.json`, `rest_position_list.json`, `rest_execution_list.json`, `rest_order_history.json`, plus private-WS sequences `ws_partial_fill.jsonl`, `ws_amend_reject.jsonl`, `ws_cancel_race.jsonl`, `ws_out_of_order_fills.jsonl`, `ws_duplicate_exec.jsonl`, `ws_post_terminal_push.jsonl`.
- Error fixtures for each retCode E29 maps: 10001 duplicate, 10002 clock drift, 10006, 10018, 110001, 110017, 110020, 110025, 110072, plus an HTTP 5xx and a post-send timeout.
- A traceability table mapping each fixture to the transition rule (S1-S9) and the acceptance scenario it exercises.

## Out of scope
Writing the automation itself (E29-Q02), perf scripts (E29-Q03), chaos orchestration (E29-Q04), the a11y audit (E29-Q05). Fan-out and algo fixtures (E33/E34 extend this set).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every story is covered
  Then the plan contains at least one black-box case for every acceptance scenario in E29-S01 through E29-S08, referenced by scenario name

Scenario: Every transition rule has a fixture
  Then each of the binding transition rules S1 through S9 in 24-internal-schemas.md section 8.2 maps to at least one named fixture

Scenario: Fixtures are deterministic
  When any fixture is replayed twice against the mock exchange
  Then the resulting OMS state is identical both times

Scenario: An unobservable transition is a defect
  Given a state transition that cannot be observed through the API, WS stream or diagnostics endpoint
  Then it is recorded as a gap and a diagnostics ticket is filed against E29-T08
```

## Technical notes / design
Fixtures are captured from the real Bybit **demo** environment through the E08 adapter's recording mode and then redacted: API keys, signatures and account UIDs are replaced with stable synthetic values by a `scrub_fixture()` helper, with a CI check that no fixture contains a string matching the key or signature patterns. Each fixture carries a header comment naming its source date, symbol and the rule it exercises. The mock exchange serving them is the fixture-replay server from `03-testing-strategy.md` section 4.1.

## Test plan
The plan is itself reviewed rather than executed: QA lead review plus an Architect review of the fixture-to-rule mapping. A CI job asserts every fixture parses against the documented Bybit response schema and that the scrubber leaves no credential-shaped strings.

## Security notes
Recorded fixtures are the classic accidental-secret-leak vector. The scrubber plus the CI secret-scan on `packages/fixtures/**` is mandatory before any fixture is committed. Fixtures are demo-environment only; capturing live-account fixtures is prohibited.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes the keyboard-only and screen-reader charters that E29-Q05 later executes formally.

## Performance notes
N/A for the plan; perf thresholds are referenced, not measured here.

## Observability
Gaps found (transitions not observable) are filed against E29-T08 so the metric and diagnostics surface grows to cover them.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact (plan / suite / script / report) merged under `tests/` or `docs/qa/` and runnable from CI or documented as an on-demand job.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the story or task it verifies, by ticket key.

title: Automate the E2E and contract suites for the OMS lifecycle and blotters
body:
## Context
R3's E2E gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4) requires Playwright coverage on web **and** Electron for the trading surfaces, and the contract gate requires "contract tests on every order/position event shape". E29 owns the order/position/execution shapes everything else builds on, so its suites become the regression floor for E30-E34.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright suite `tests/e2e/oms/` running against a backend wired to the fixture-replay mock exchange, executed in both the web and Electron projects: full lifecycle (place, partial fill, amend, cancel), blotter grouping/filtering, inline amend accept and reject, cancel-all with partial failure, partial close including the dust path, reconnect with a correction summary, and manager-scope negative cases.
- Contract tests: every WS private payload (`orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`) validated against its `cv://ws/v1/*.schema.json`; every E29 REST route validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml` in both directions (request and response), failing CI on drift.
- A state-machine conformance test driving the fixtures from E29-Q01 through the public API and asserting the observable state sequence for rules S1-S9.
- Test-data helpers: session factories for owner, manager (single account) and viewer roles.
- CI wiring: the suite runs on every PR touching `area/oms-execution` paths and nightly in full.

## Out of scope
Perf and load (E29-Q03), chaos (E29-Q04), a11y (E29-Q05), fan-out and algo E2E (E33/E34), live-environment runs (forbidden until R4).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Lifecycle end to end on both shells
  When the lifecycle spec runs in the web project and in the Electron project
  Then both pass with identical assertions and no shell-specific skips

Scenario: Contract drift fails the build
  Given a WS payload field is renamed without updating its schema
  Then the contract test fails with the offending field named

Scenario: Manager scope negative case
  Given a manager session granted only account B
  When the suite requests account A orders, positions and executions over REST and WS
  Then each returns 403 or a narrowed result, no A data appears, and an audit row exists

Scenario: Flake budget
  Given the suite runs 20 consecutive times in CI
  Then the flake rate is below 1% and any flaky spec is quarantined with a ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
No `sleep`-based waits: every assertion waits on an application signal (a WS frame applied, a state attribute set) exposed through `data-testid` and a test-only readiness event. The mock exchange is driven through an HTTP control plane so a spec can inject a rejection or a disconnect at an exact point in the lifecycle. Electron runs use the same specs with the Playwright Electron launcher to prove no shell-specific regression.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* test code; its own verification is a 20-run stability soak in CI plus a mutation check - deliberately breaking three known behaviours (amend-reject restores prior values, dust guard, manager scope) and confirming the suite fails each time.

## Security notes
The suite includes the RBAC negative matrix for E29 routes (owner, manager, viewer against every route), which is the evidence for R3 exit criterion 10 for this epic's surface. Test credentials are demo-only and injected from CI secrets, never committed.

## Accessibility notes
Each E2E spec ends with an axe-core scan of the screen it exercised, so a11y regressions surface with the functional run; the full audit remains E29-Q05.

## Performance notes
Suite wall-clock target <=12 minutes on the PR path through sharding; the nightly full run has no cap.

## Observability
CI publishes a per-scenario pass/fail report and a trend of flake rate; failures attach the Playwright trace and the mock-exchange transcript.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact (plan / suite / script / report) merged under `tests/` or `docs/qa/` and runnable from CI or documented as an on-demand job.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the story or task it verifies, by ticket key.

title: Build the k6 load scripts proving budget #4 and the blotter frame budget
body:
## Context
Budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.2) is a **hard gate** for R3: order submit to ack p95 <300 ms on demo with the backend-added portion isolated and asserted <=50 ms p95. R3's load gate additionally requires "sustained order flow at the per-UID limit across 5 accounts for 1 h with zero lost acknowledgements and correct governor back-off". The client side has its own budget: SCR-063 at 500 rows / 60 fps with position updates coalesced at 10 Hz.

## Scope / Deliverables
- k6 script `tests/load/oms_submit_ack.js`: order submit flow against (a) the fixture-replay mock for pure backend-overhead isolation and (b) Bybit demo for the end-to-end figure, reporting p50/p95/p99 for both totals and the backend-added portion derived from the `order_submit_seconds` histogram.
- k6 script `tests/load/oms_sustained_flow.js`: 1 h sustained flow across 5 demo accounts at the per-UID limit, asserting zero lost acknowledgements (every submitted `order_link_id` reaches a terminal or known state) and correct 10018 back-off behaviour.
- A blotter frontend benchmark (`tests/perf/blotter.bench.ts`) driving 500 position rows and 1 000 order rows with a scripted 10 Hz update stream, asserting p95 frame time and scripting time per frame apply.
- A results template recorded on the epic and fed into the R3 composite capacity scenario (section 5 of the standard).

## Out of scope
Fan-out overhead measurement beyond 5 accounts (E34 owns the fan-out sub-clause), engine FPS for chart layers (E11/E46), the full composite capacity run (owned by the R3 gate, this feeds it).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Backend-added overhead is isolated and within budget
  When the submit script runs against the fixture-replay mock
  Then the backend-added portion is p95 <=50 ms and is reported separately from exchange RTT

Scenario: End-to-end demo budget
  When the submit script runs against Bybit demo
  Then submit to ack is p95 <300 ms and the run records p50, p95 and p99

Scenario: Nothing is lost under sustained flow
  Given 1 h of sustained order flow across 5 demo accounts at the per-UID limit
  Then every submitted order_link_id ends in a known state, oms_unknown_orders returns to zero, and 10018 responses produce back-off rather than retry storms

Scenario: Blotter holds its frame budget
  Given 500 position rows updating at 10 Hz
  Then p95 frame time stays <=16.6 ms and the run reports scripting time per frame apply
```

## Technical notes / design
The backend-added portion is measured from the server histogram rather than subtracted from wall clock, so network variance cannot hide a regression. Demo runs use small quantities on demo accounts and are rate-limited by the governor under test - the script must not itself bypass the budget. The frontend benchmark drives the real store and renderer through a scripted WS transcript so the measurement includes frame apply, not just paint.

## Test plan
Self-verifying: each script asserts its own thresholds and fails the job when breached. A calibration run with an artificial 100 ms delay injected into the backend proves the scripts actually detect a regression.

## Security notes
Load scripts hold demo credentials from CI secrets only; running them against live is blocked by an environment guard that refuses any base URL that is not the demo host. Generated order volume is bounded so a misconfigured run cannot exhaust the demo account.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user-facing surface.

## Performance notes
This ticket is the budget-#4 evidence for the R3 gate; results are archived per run so a trend, not just a snapshot, is available at the gate.

## Observability
Results are pushed as CI artefacts and as Prometheus recording rules so `order_submit_seconds` p95 is dashboarded continuously rather than only during a load run.

title: Build the chaos scenarios for lost acks, reconnect storms and Postgres failover
body:
## Context
ADR-0006's whole justification is what happens when acknowledgements are lost, and R3's chaos gate requires "WS kill mid-order, backend restart mid-TWAP, Postgres failover mid-fan-out - all resume to a correct, reconciled state". E29 owns the first and third of those and the recovery machinery the other two depend on. A chaos suite that only proves the app survives is insufficient: it must prove the *book* is correct afterwards.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Chaos harness `tests/chaos/oms/` with injectable faults through the mock exchange control plane and container orchestration: post-send timeout, duplicate ack, out-of-order fills, post-terminal push, private-WS kill mid-lifecycle, backend SIGKILL mid-submission, Postgres failover mid-transaction, 10002 clock drift, 10018 IP rate limit.
- A correctness oracle run after every scenario: local order and position state is compared field by field against the mock/demo exchange truth, and any difference fails the scenario.
- Scenario: crash between a partial-close fill and the protective resize (E29-S03) - on restart the resize must complete and the position must not be left with an over-sized stop.
- Scenario: `Unknown` resolution - a lost ack must resolve by reconciliation only, with an assertion that **zero** resubmissions were sent (counted at the mock exchange).
- Scenario: two consecutive reconciliation passes finding nothing must transition to `Rejected` with `UNRESOLVED_AFTER_RECONCILE`.
- Runbook notes for each scenario: what the operator sees, which alert fires, expected recovery time.

## Out of scope
Fan-out unwind chaos (E34), algo resume chaos (E33), exchange-wide outage simulation (E45), Tailscale/network-layer faults (E45).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A lost acknowledgement never duplicates
  Given the transport times out after the exchange accepted the order
  Then the order enters Unknown, the reconciler resolves it to its true state, and the mock exchange recorded exactly one create request

Scenario: Crash mid-partial-close
  Given the backend is killed between the reducing fill and the protective resize
  When it restarts
  Then the protective stop is resized to the remaining position within the recovery window and no over-sized stop persists

Scenario: Postgres failover
  Given Postgres fails over during a submission
  Then order entry is refused while it is unavailable, no order is accepted that was not durably recorded, and after recovery the book matches the exchange

Scenario: Post-terminal push
  Given the exchange pushes an update for an order already in a terminal state
  Then the order is not mutated, a ReconcileAnomaly is audited and alerted

Scenario: The oracle is authoritative
  Then every scenario ends with a field-by-field comparison against exchange truth and fails on any difference
```

## Technical notes / design
Faults are injected deterministically at named lifecycle points rather than by random timing, so a failure is reproducible from the scenario name alone. The resubmission counter lives at the mock exchange, not in the app, so "no blind resubmission" is proven from outside. Postgres failover uses a two-node test topology in the compose profile; the assertion is on behaviour (refuse to accept), not on failover speed.

## Test plan
Each scenario runs in CI nightly and as a required check before the R3 gate. A meta-test deliberately disables the reconciler and asserts every relevant scenario fails - proving the suite has teeth.

## Security notes
Chaos runs use demo accounts only, guarded by the same environment check as the load scripts. Fault injection endpoints exist only in the test profile and are compiled out of production images, verified by a CI check that the production image does not expose the control plane.

## Accessibility notes
The scenarios assert the user-facing consequences from E29-S07 (controls disabled, banner state, summary contents) so the recovery UX is chaos-verified, not just the backend.

## Performance notes
Recovery-time expectations are recorded per scenario: reconciliation resolves an Unknown order within one cycle (<=30 s) and time-to-usable after a 30 s outage is <=5 s.

## Observability
Each scenario asserts the expected metric and alert fired: `oms_unknown_orders` rising then returning to zero, `oms_reconcile_corrections_total` incrementing, `naked_position_alerts_total` for the over-sized/absent stop case.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact (plan / suite / script / report) merged under `tests/` or `docs/qa/` and runnable from CI or documented as an on-demand job.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the story or task it verifies, by ticket key.

title: Run the accessibility audit of the blotters, fills detail and reconciliation states
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8 makes WCAG 2.2 AA default-on for every UI surface with no internal-tool exception, and the R3 a11y gate names the danger/confirm patterns specifically. SCR-063 is the hardest a11y surface in this epic: a virtualised grid with live-updating rows, per-row destructive actions and a banner that must announce once without chattering.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A formal audit of SCR-063 (all tabs), SCR-078 and the SCR-152 states, covering: keyboard-only operation of every control, screen-reader passes with NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS, focus order and visible focus, target sizes, contrast including the liq-proximity and PnL treatments, and reduced-motion behaviour.
- Verification of the windowed-grid rules in `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 6.1: roving tabindex stability across virtualisation, position-in-set announcements, and that scrolling does not strand focus.
- Verification of the live-region policy: order state changes announce politely and debounced; the reconnect countdown does **not** announce on every tick; `role="alert"` fires once per state entry.
- Verification that no status is colour-only anywhere: side, order state, liq-proximity, PnL sign, maker/taker, provisional PnL.
- Findings filed as Bugs with `priority/*` and a re-test pass after fixes; an audit report in `docs/qa/e29-a11y-audit.md`.

## Out of scope
The order ticket, chart trading and DOM surfaces (E30/E31 run their own audits), the chart canvas keyboard model beyond execution marks (E11/E47), the epic-wide a11y sweep at R5 (E47).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Keyboard-only completion
  Given only a keyboard
  Then every blotter task can be completed: switch tabs, sort, filter, group, open a row menu, amend, cancel, partial close, export, and open the detail drawer

Scenario: Screen-reader comprehension
  When a screen-reader user reviews the positions tab
  Then account, symbol, side, quantity and liq-proximity are all conveyed without relying on colour and the totals row is identified as a total

Scenario: The banner does not chatter
  Given the reconnecting banner with a live countdown
  Then the state is announced once and the countdown is not announced on each tick

Scenario: axe-core is clean
  Then axe-core reports zero violations of serious or critical impact on SCR-063, SCR-078 and every SCR-152 state

Scenario: Findings are closed
  Then every finding is fixed or filed with a priority label and the re-test pass is recorded
```

## Technical notes / design
Automated axe-core runs are necessary but not sufficient - the virtualisation, live-region and focus-management defects this surface is prone to are invisible to axe, so the manual passes are the substance of the ticket. Each state is forced through the fixture-replay mock and feature flags rather than by hand-editing the DOM, so the audited rendering is the real one.

## Test plan
Audit execution is the work; its output is the report plus filed bugs. A regression guard is added to E29-Q02 so each E2E spec ends with an axe scan, preventing silent regression between audits.

## Security notes
Verify that assistive-technology exposure does not leak out-of-scope data - e.g. a manager's screen reader must not be able to reach hidden rows for accounts outside the grant (they must be absent from the DOM, not merely hidden).

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the accessibility verification; findings map to `05-accessibility-standard.md` clause numbers so remediation is unambiguous.

## Performance notes
Confirm that live-region and announcement handling does not itself breach the 500-row / 60 fps budget - announcement debouncing must not be implemented with per-frame DOM writes.

## Observability
Audit findings are tracked to closure on the epic; the axe regression guard reports per-screen violation counts as a CI trend.

title: Execute the exploratory charters, assemble the regression pack and record E29 QA sign-off
body:
## Context
The epic DoD requires "an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA". E29 is also the first epic whose regression pack every later trading epic inherits, so the pack must be curated rather than accumulated: the scenarios that would catch a book-correctness regression, runnable in under an hour.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Execution of the exploratory charters from E29-Q01 as time-boxed, session-based testing with session notes per charter.
- A curated regression pack `docs/qa/e29-regression-pack.md` plus the CI tag `@oms-regression` applied to the E2E specs that constitute it: full lifecycle, amend-reject, cancel race, partial close with dust, manager scope, reconnect with correction, untracked adoption.
- A 48 h continuous demo run (place, partial fill, amend, cancel, close on a schedule) with a daily book-correctness comparison against the exchange, feeding the R3 7-day soak.
- Defect triage: every finding filed with priority, P0/P1 closed before sign-off.
- The QA sign-off comment on E29 with pass/fail per story and an explicit statement of any deviation.

## Out of scope
The R3 7-day soak itself (train-level, `30-release-roadmap.md` section 12 `q09`), fan-out and algo regression (E33/E34 extend the pack), the PRR.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Charters executed
  Then every exploratory charter has session notes recording what was tried, what was observed and what was filed

Scenario: The regression pack is fast and meaningful
  Given the @oms-regression tag is run
  Then it completes in under one hour and covers every book-correctness scenario listed in the pack

Scenario: 48 h continuous run is clean
  Given a 48 h scheduled demo lifecycle run
  Then local state matches the exchange at every daily comparison and oms_unknown_orders is zero at the end of each day

Scenario: Sign-off is conditional on defects
  Given an open P0 or P1 against E29 scope
  Then QA sign-off is withheld and the blocking defect is named on the epic
```

The 48 h run uses tiny quantities on a dedicated demo account and is driven by the same harness as the load scripts, with the governor active so it exercises the real rate-budget path. The book comparison reuses the E29-Q04 correctness oracle rather than a second implementation.

## Test plan
This ticket executes tests rather than adding them; its verification is the recorded evidence - session notes, run logs, comparison reports, and the sign-off comment.

## Security notes
Sign-off explicitly checks that the RBAC negative matrix for E29 routes passed (R3 exit criterion 10 for this surface) and that no fixture or log captured during the run contains credential material.

## Accessibility notes
Sign-off is conditional on E29-Q05 being closed with no open serious or critical findings.

## Performance notes

The 48 h run's metrics are retained as the baseline profile for the epic: submit latency distribution, reconcile correction rate, unknown-order count.
