title: Produce the STRIDE threat model for the OMS and its order-placement path
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4 names E29 as one of six epics requiring a STRIDE model with **all Critical/High findings closed** before the R3 gate, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.1 requires the model to be kicked off at epic start for anything touching the OMS. The OMS is the component that turns a request into money moving, so the model must be finished before E29-T04 (the submission pipeline) merges - it is a design input, not a review artefact.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model in `docs/security/e29-oms-threat-model.md` with a data-flow diagram covering: client -> REST `/orders` -> RiskGate -> OMS -> RateBudget -> BybitAdapter -> Bybit, and Bybit private WS -> OMS -> Postgres -> WS fan-out -> client.
- Threats enumerated per STRIDE category per element and per data flow, each with a rating, a control, and the ticket that implements the control. At minimum: spoofed order origin; tampering with quantity or account between client and OMS; repudiation of a placed or cancelled order; cross-account information disclosure through REST, WS subscription or execution marks; denial of service by order flooding or by exhausting a UID's rate budget with background traffic; elevation of privilege through a manager acting on an unt granted account or through the `untracked` adoption path.
- Explicit analysis of the idempotency key as a security control: what an attacker who can predict or replay an `order_link_id` can do, and why the collision check and the persisted-before-send rule bound it.
- Analysis of `order_events.payload` as a credential-leak channel and the redaction requirement it produces.
- Abuse cases handed to E29-X02, and any control gap filed as a ticket before the model is signed off.

## Out of scope
Key storage and envelope encryption (E27's model), fan-out unwind threats (E34), rule-engine sandbox threats (E35), kill-switch bypass (E39), penetration testing (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Complete coverage
  Then every element and data flow in the diagram has each of the six STRIDE categories either addressed with a control or explicitly argued not applicable

Scenario: Controls are traceable
  Then every Critical or High threat names the ticket implementing its control and that ticket references this model

Scenario: The model gates the pipeline
  Given E29-T04 is ready to merge
  Then this model is complete and its Critical/High controls are either implemented or scheduled with an agreed date

Scenario: Idempotency is analysed as a control
  Then the model states what an attacker who replays or predicts an order_link_id can and cannot achieve
```

## Technical notes / design
The model uses the data-flow decomposition already in `24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.4 rather than inventing a parallel one, so the diagram and the implementation cannot drift. Ratings use the programme's standard likelihood/impact matrix from `04-security-program.md`. Where a control lives in another epic (RBAC in E09, keys in E27, risk caps in E39), the model records the dependency explicitly instead of restating the control.

## Test plan
Reviewed by the Security engineer and the Architect; each Critical/High control is later evidenced by a test in E29-X02 or in the story that implements it. The model is re-reviewed at the R3 gate as part of the continuous OMS threat-model refresh cadence (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 12 bar `s05`).

## Security notes
This ticket is the security artefact. Data classification for the whole epic is set here: financial/restricted for orders, positions and executions; secret for anything in `order_events.payload` before redaction.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - documentation.

## Performance notes
Notes the DoS-relevant budget interactions: the protective reserve in the rate budget is a security control as well as a safety one, because it prevents a flood of normal traffic from starving a stop-loss.

## Observability
Names the audit and metric signals each threat relies on for detection: `oms_unknown_orders`, `oms_rate_reject_total`, the audit rows for every mutation, and alerting on cross-scope 403s.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact merged (threat model in `docs/security/`, rules under `.semgrep/` or the CI config, tests under `tests/security/`).
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding either fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off recorded (R3 gate, `30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4).

title: Implement the abuse-case suite, RBAC scope assertions and SAST rules for the OMS
body:
## Context
E29-X01 produces the threats; this ticket turns them into executable, permanently-running checks. R3 exit criterion 10 requires "an automated matrix test exercising every route by every role, asserting 403, no state change and an audit row for every disallowed combination" - for the OMS routes, that test is built here. `04-security-program.md` additionally requires SAST rules to encode project-specific invariants rather than relying on generic rulesets alone.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Abuse-case suite `tests/security/oms/`: manager acting on a non-granted account over REST and over WS subscribe; viewer attempting every mutating route; forged `order_link_id` replay; client-supplied quantity larger than the position on close; `reduce_only` stripped in transit; an out-of-scope account id smuggled in a batch or filter parameter; order flooding to exhaust a UID budget and the assertion that protective traffic still gets a token; submission attempted while an account is marked stale; submission attempted while Postgres is unavailable.
- RBAC route-by-role matrix covering every E29 REST route and every private WS topic, asserting status, absence of state change and presence of an audit row.
- Semgrep/Bandit rules under `.semgrep/oms.yml`: forbid `float(` on monetary values in OMS modules; forbid an unscoped `select(orders|positions|executions)` helper; forbid writing `order_events.payload` without passing it through `redact_exchange_payload()`; forbid any exchange call outside the adapter package; forbid environment conditionals (`if env == "live"`) outside `ExchangeCapabilities`.
- Secret-scanning coverage extended to `packages/fixtures/**` and to test artefacts.
- A CI job running the suite on every PR touching `area/oms-execution`.

## Out of scope
DAST/ZAP scanning (programme-level, `s06`), dependency scanning (programme-level), penetration testing (E43), key-vault abuse cases (E27), kill-switch bypass tests (E39).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every disallowed combination is proven
  Given every E29 route and WS topic crossed with owner, manager and viewer roles
  When the matrix runs
  Then each disallowed combination returns 403, changes no state, and writes an audit row

Scenario: Replay of an idempotency key cannot create a second order
  Given a captured order_link_id
  When it is replayed
  Then the exchange duplicate rejection triggers success-after-lookup and no second order exists

Scenario: The protective reserve cannot be starved
  Given normal-priority traffic saturating a UID rate budget
  When a stop-loss placement is requested
  Then it acquires a token from the reserve and succeeds

Scenario: SAST rules have teeth
  Given a deliberately introduced float conversion on a monetary value in an OMS module
  Then the Semgrep rule fails the build naming the file and line

Scenario: No credential reaches storage
  Given an exchange response containing signature and key headers
  When it is written to order_events.payload
  Then the stored payload contains neither, verified by an automated test
```

## Technical notes / design
The RBAC matrix is generated from the OpenAPI document's `x-rbac` annotations rather than hand-listed, so a new route without an annotation fails the test - making the matrix self-maintaining as E30-E34 add routes. Abuse cases run against the fixture-replay mock so they are deterministic and safe to run on every PR. Rate-budget starvation is tested against the real token-bucket implementation, not a stub.

## Test plan
The suite is the test; its own credibility is established with negative controls - temporarily removing a scope check, the redaction call and the reserve, and confirming the corresponding case fails each time.

## Security notes
This ticket is the primary evidence for the R3 security gate on this epic. Findings feed E29-X03. Any case that cannot be automated is recorded as a manual check on the X03 checklist rather than silently dropped.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI surface, though the suite asserts that out-of-scope rows are **absent** from responses rather than merely hidden, which is also an a11y-relevant property (a screen reader must not reach them).

## Performance notes
The suite must stay under 5 minutes on the PR path; the rate-budget starvation case uses a compressed bucket configuration rather than real-time waiting.

## Observability
Asserts that each refused attempt produces the expected audit row and increments `rbac_denied_total{route,role}`, so abuse is detectable in production and not only in tests.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact merged (threat model in `docs/security/`, rules under `.semgrep/` or the CI config, tests under `tests/security/`).
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding either fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off recorded (R3 gate, `30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4).
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present on this ticket and on the tickets it gates.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk was surfaced or an existing one retired.

title: Security review and sign-off of the shipped OMS
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8 makes a Security engineer sign-off mandatory for the order-placement path regardless of labelling, and the R3 gate requires all Critical/High STRIDE findings closed for E29 before the train can complete. This is the closing review: code review of the security-relevant paths, verification that each modelled control actually shipped, and the recorded sign-off.

## Scope / Deliverables
- White-box review of the security-relevant code: the submission pipeline's authorisation and scoping, `order_link_id` generation and collision handling, the redaction of `order_events.payload`, the rate-budget reserve, the reconciliation adoption path (`untracked` orders must never become rule-managed), and the WS subscription narrowing.
- Verification that every Critical/High threat from E29-X01 has a shipped control and a passing test, with the evidence linked per threat.
- Execution of the manual abuse checks that E29-X02 could not automate, recorded on a checklist.
- Confirmation that no secret material appears in logs, metrics labels, diagnostics payloads, audit rows, error messages or fixtures - sampled from a real 48 h demo run (E29-Q06).
- Confirmation that the live transport path remains structurally unreachable: no code path can reach live while the R4 gate is off, verified by inspection of the capability wiring and by a test.
- The sign-off comment on E29 with any accepted risks named and Owner-signed.

## Out of scope
Penetration testing (E43), live-enablement gating implementation (E44), remediating findings (filed as their own tickets against the owning story).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every modelled control shipped
  Then each Critical or High threat in the E29 threat model links to shipped code and a passing test

Scenario: No secret leaks
  Given logs, metrics, diagnostics payloads, audit rows and fixtures from a 48 h demo run
  When they are sampled and scanned
  Then no API key, signature or other credential material is found

Scenario: Live is structurally unreachable
  Given the R4 live gate is off
  Then no code path can submit an order to the live environment, proven by inspection and by an automated test

Scenario: Untracked orders stay unmanaged
  Given an order adopted as untracked during reconciliation
  Then no rule or algo can act on it, asserted by test

Scenario: Sign-off is recorded
  Then a Security engineer sign-off comment exists on E29 with any accepted risks named and Owner-signed
```

## Technical notes / design
The review follows the threat model element by element rather than file by file, so coverage is argued rather than assumed. Accepted risks must state the compensating control and an expiry - an accepted risk with no review date is not accepted.

## Test plan
Review activity, evidenced by the completed checklist, linked test runs and the sign-off comment. Any finding becomes a ticket on the owning story with a priority label, and P0/P1 findings block the epic's Done.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security gate for the epic. It also feeds the continuous OMS threat-model refresh running across S14-S19 and hands its open items to E43's hardening backlog.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - review activity.

## Performance notes
Confirms that no security control was disabled or weakened to meet budget #4 - specifically that validation, scoping and audit writes are all inside the measured path rather than deferred out of it.

## Observability
Confirms the detection signals exist and alert correctly: `rbac_denied_total`, `oms_unknown_orders` paging, audit rows on every mutation, and that the audit hash chain covers OMS events.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact merged (threat model in `docs/security/`, rules under `.semgrep/` or the CI config, tests under `tests/security/`).
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding either fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off recorded (R3 gate, `30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4).
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present on this ticket and on the tickets it gates.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk was surfaced or an existing one retired.
- [ ] PR merged through the merge queue with required approvals and checks.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E29-X02 (the automated evidence), E29-Q04 (chaos results demonstrating recovery correctness), E29-Q06 (the 48 h run sampled for secret leakage).
